title: Senior Full Stack Engineer
description:
Updated in October 2026 

Target start date: March 1, 2027 

Compensation: 70,000 to 85,000 EUR yearly gross, depending on profile 

Location: Either in-office in Paris (Grands Boulevards, 75002) or full remote on Paris timezone 

About Upflow 

Upflow is the Financial Relationship Management (FRM) platform that helps B2B finance teams collect smarter and get paid by their customers faster, with AI agents working alongside the team.

Today, the order-to-cash process is mission critical for businesses, yet it remains fragmented across tools, teams, and workflows. Upflow brings this entire process into one system — four products covering the cycle from invoice to cash (Insights, Collections, Payments, and Cash Application), with AI agents that work alongside the team and a shared intelligence layer underneath.

We serve 500+ companies across 30+ countries, including Vercel, Lattice, and Productboard, and are backed by leading investors including Y Combinator, Hedosophia, Hexa, and Lorimer. With teams across the US and Europe, we're building a category-defining company at the intersection of finance, payments, and AI.

To learn more about what we do, visit upflow.io .

For a behind-the-scenes look at how we work as a team, head to the Inside Upflow section of our blog at upflow.io/blog/inside-upflow 

About the role 

You’ll join a small, efficient team who builds high-impact features for our users. You'll work on a wide range of topics, including AI agents, workflow automations, analytics, or payment processing. We invest significantly in AI features, and you'll play a key role in making Upflow the leading agentic software in our field.

We work at a fast pace, averaging 20 deploys to production each day, but with high quality standards, and we value pragmatism, ownership, and a growth mindset.

AI is also transforming how we work, and we're looking for someone eager to use and optimize agents to help us work more efficiently.

You can be based in our Paris office or work remotely.

What you will do 

In your day-to-day, you will:

- Architect and implement complex, high-impact product features from start-to-finish.

- Collaborate closely with the product manager, the designer, and other engineers to translate business requirements into technical solutions.

- Ship clean, maintainable code to production daily.

- Participate actively in technical reviews providing and receiving constructive feedback.

- Troubleshoot and debug complex product issues.

- Optimize application performance and ensure scalability.

- Help improve our agentic tools and automations.

Our current stack 

- Frontend: Typescript, React, GraphQL

- Backend: Typescript, Node.js, Express, Postgres, and Redis

- Infra: GCP, Terraform

- Observability: Datadog and Sentry

- Github, Copilot, Claude Code, CircleCI

Who you are 

- You have 5+ years of experience in software engineering.

- You have strong proficiency in Typescript, React and SQL.

- You’re proficient at working with agentic coding assistant such as Claude Code.

- You have strong skills in architecture, software reliability, and scalability

- You have a product sensibility and care about UX.

- You have good teamwork skills and enjoy providing and receiving feedback.

- You want to work in a startup environment that values excellence, autonomy, and ownership.

- You are fluent in English with strong communication skills.

- You are based in Paris, or live in Paris timezone

Why join us 

- International mindset : We have offices in Paris and New York.

- On-site or full remote : On-site job in Paris (2-3 days in office), or full remote position on Paris timezone (1 monthly visit in our Paris office).

- Exciting moment : Opportunity to contribute to the Engineering function in the AI era.

- All-star team : Extremely solid team with deep functional and domain expertise.

- Learning opportunity : Strong focus on learning and growing through education and professional development.

- Trusting environment : Hands-off management style. We have a strong culture of ownership and autonomy.

- Best in class perks : 35 paid days off, meal vouchers, cool offices, top-of-the-range equipment, great healthcare, and competitive salary and equity

- Offsites : Regular offsites with the team, meetups, and strong connections to the startup ecosystem.

Recruitment Process 

1 - Screening call 

It’s a discussion with your future manager. We’ll get deeper into your expertise and know-how. We’ll also give you a clearer view of what your day-to-day in that role is like. It’s a good opportunity to see if you foresee yourself working at Upflow.

2 - Take home assignment 

It’s a coding exercise that can only be completed successfully with the help of AI. In addition to delivering working software that meets the requirements, you’ll be evaluated on your product and architectural decisions.

3 - Technical interview 

In this interview, we’ll review your take-home assignment and discuss how you approach designing scalable systems and making architectural decisions.

4 - Meet the team! 

You’ll also meet up with at least two other peers so you can foresee yourself as part of this team. 

5 - Founder interview 

Meet with Alex (co-founder & CEO). He will tell you everything about Upflow’s vision and values. It’s a privileged moment to ask questions, too.

6 - Alignment and offer 

If the team meetings go well on both sides, we’ll invite you to this final step. Getting here means we both see a strong fit and believe Upflow is a place where you can grow and shine over the next few years. We’ll align on how you’ll join us (role scope, start date, package), and if we’re all on the same page, we’ll extend you an offer!

***** 

Diversity & Inclusion 

At Upflow, we are committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. We encourage all individuals to apply, even if you don’t meet every qualification. Research shows that some candidates may hesitate to apply unless they meet every requirement. However, we believe that a variety of experiences and perspectives can bring value beyond the listed qualifications. If you’re excited about what we do and feel you could contribute, we want to hear from you.

You might know us as ZnanyLekarz in Poland or Doctoralia in Spain. Globally, we are Docplanner .

We build technology that helps people live longer, healthier lives. Our products connect patients with doctors, power clinical workflows, and support healthcare systems used by millions of people every month. 

Engineering at Docplanner is about building reliable, scalable systems with real human impact. What we ship affects patients, doctors, and clinics in everyday, high-stakes situations - which means quality, judgment, and long-term thinking matter.

In 2026, we are accelerating delivery across multiple product areas by changing how we build - leveraging AI-assisted development to increase engineering effectiveness and raise the bar on how we design, ship, and evolve systems.

And why should you join us? 

Because it feels good to tell your family and your friends how you made the world a little bit better. You go to bed knowing that what you do matters, and that your talents align with your beliefs.

We want to help people live longer, healthier lives, and that starts with you being you. We believe that taking the diversity of human experience into account makes a better healthcare experience for all . We’re not just different: we embrace diversity. We will encourage you to come to work your whole self. You can decide to work fully remote, or work hybrid with our offices located in Barcelona or Warsaw. This will be dependent on the final team allocation. 

Our challenges 

Our Engineers may join teams working on these areas and challenges:

Marketplace & Search 

Build the next-generation marketplace system by owning the end-to-end journey from agentic discovery to rebooking. You’ll leverage AI search and AI onboarding funnels to unlock new demand and transform one-off bookings into continuous care loops.

Practice Management Systems (PMS) 

Build the next generation of software to help doctors globally. Unify the current fragmented reality and leverage AI to reinvent the way to help doctors focus on what matters most: treating the patient.

AI-powered Clinical Tools (Noa Medic) 

Design AI-native clinical workflows that move beyond simple scribing to replace end-to-end administrative tasks. You'll build deep PMS/EHR embeddings that become an indispensable daily habit for medical professionals.

Patient & Data Integrations (Noa Patient) 

Move beyond the booking button to build a proactive healthcare partner. You'll create the smart connections that blend someone's medical past with their live health data, crafting an AI experience that actually keeps patients coming back. Turn raw data into advice people can use, making Docplanner the one health app they can't live without.

Internally, these challenges map to some of our most ambitious and high-impact initiatives.

How we build software 

- 
We build systems that matter and we optimize for clarity, speed, and long-term maintainability.

- 
Small autonomous teams that own real product surfaces end-to-end

- 
High trust and high ownership from day one

- 
Production impact early - even as a junior engineer

- 
AI-assisted development as a default workflow

- 
Strong engineering culture focused on simplicity, correctness, and measurable outcomes

- 
We prefer solving problems well over adding unnecessary complexity.

- 
Good ideas win regardless of tenure or hierarchy.

What we value 

Strong problem solving ability. The ability to break down complex systems and find elegant solutions.

Builder mindset. You like creating things that people use.

Intellectual curiosity. You enjoy understanding how systems really work.

Ownership. You treat problems as yours until they are solved.

Pragmatism. You know when to optimize and when to ship.

We value signals over credentials.

Competition programming, open-source work, research, side projects or anything else that shows how you think.

Technical Environment 

- 
Our stack evolves continuously, but currently includes technologies such as:

- 
Backend: Node.js, TypeScript

- 
Frontend: React, TypeScript

title: Software Engineer, Web (Full stack)
description:
We are looking for someone to join us as an early member of the Web team, to build and own web platforms that turn large amounts of data into products people love to use. Maps and location data sit at the core of what we build, and we’re looking for an engineer who can take a platform from data model to pixel.

In the initial months, you’ll work closely with the team, gradually taking ownership of central systems and features. Given our stage, we’re seeking versatile engineers comfortable contributing across the frontend, the backend and the data.

We value team members who delve deep into their respective domains, aiming to cultivate a team of subject matter experts with a high sense of ownership. This commitment to expertise is an expectation for every team member.

As a Web Engineer, your day-to-day will include: 

Platform Engineering 

Designing and building robust, scalable web platforms end-to-end in TypeScript: APIs, services, data access layers and the UI on top of them. You’ll make the architectural decisions and set the patterns that others build on.

Workflows & Data Pipelines 

Architecting durable, long-running workflows and background processes on our workflow orchestration system (Restate). You’ll also build the pipelines that move data between our warehouse, our databases and our products, reliably and at scale.

Data Modeling & Visualization 

Modeling large datasets so they can be queried and visualized fast. That includes choosing the right aggregations, pre-computations and storage across Postgres and BigQuery, and turning them into visualizations that are clear, interactive and beautiful. You’ll handle data with privacy in mind from the very first design decision.

Maps & Geospatial Data 

Bringing geospatial data to life on the web. You’ll render large amounts of location data on interactive maps, and keep them as fast and polished as they are insightful.

Roadmap Creation and Ideation 

Contributing actively to the roadmap: identifying the right tradeoffs and bringing ideas from both a product and an engineering perspective.

Owning your scope 

You’ll be responsible for the architecture, performance, monitoring and reliability of everything you ship. We value engineers who take full ownership of their scope, and who proactively address issues before anyone asks.

Your Skills & Experience: 

Please indicate your years of experience on the application form.

- 7+ years of professional experience building SaaS products or data-heavy platforms.

- High proficiency in TypeScript and Node.js, and in modern web frameworks (React, Next.js…).

- Strong experience with Postgres and data warehouses (BigQuery, Snowflake, or similar).

- Solid understanding of data modeling for analytics and for visualizing large volumes of data.

- A privacy-aware approach to handling sensitive data, such as aggregation and anonymization.

- Comfortable working autonomously across frontend and backend.

- Experience with workflow orchestration and long-running processes (Restate, Temporal, or similar) is a big plus.

- Expertise in map rendering and geospatial data visualization (Mapbox GL, MapLibre, deck.gl , or similar) is a big plus.

- Experience with WebGL or GPU rendering is a plus.

- Comfortable working closely with backend and data teams across a polyglot stack is a plus.

- Knowledge of infrastructure (Bazel, GCP, Kubernetes) is a plus.

- Passion and experience building great products. We’d love to hear about things you’ve shipped!

AI as a multiplier 

AI is part of how we build every day. We’re looking for engineers with a real grasp of these tools, who use them to multiply their output and not to make up for missing expertise. You should be able to drive an agent through a complex change, judge what it produces, spot where it’s subtly wrong, and stand behind every line that ships.

The bar 

We’re looking for exceptional engineers, and we set the bar high on purpose. In return, you’ll get real ownership from day one, products used by millions of people, a team that ships in days rather than quarters, a modern stack with top-tier tooling, and colleagues who will push you to grow.

You don’t need to speak French to apply (and you don’t need perfect English; we’ll help you ramp up quickly).

Life at amo: 

To ensure that everyone is set up for success within our way of working, we work together onsite 5 days a week.

We wanted to make sure coming to the office was as comfortable as possible for you:

- We chose a location in central Paris, near Opera (Metro lines 3,8,9 and RER A).

- We have a beautiful Parisian-style office with high ceilings, balconies, and huge windows. So a lot of natural light!

Because life outside of work should also be stress-free, we cover:

- Health care (100% coverage).

- Maternity Leave, Paternity Leave, Second Parent Leave (salary maintained at 100%).

- Vacation days: 8-9 weeks (total) per year - (European summer? 🥹😎).

- 5 weeks of paid time off (by the state);

title: Frontend Engineer
description:
About Shiftbase 

We build workforce software that helps people get work done. More than 10,000 companies use our platform every month to plan shifts and track time, with less admin in the way. 

We work from our Zoetermeer office with over 80 people and we grow every year. The culture is open and informal. You can push back on an idea regardless of title, and we change how we work when someone makes the case in retro. 

About the role 

You build frontend features that customers use the day you release them. You sit in a product team with backend, QA, design and product, and you take a feature from a rough product idea to a screen a planner can use without a manual. 

Your time is a balance between working on features, bugs and resolving technical debt. 

Claude Code is how our engineers write software. Everyone here uses it daily, and whole features now go out with an agent doing most of the coding. You still own what you merge, so you read the diff, you know why it works, and you can defend it in review. The interesting part of the job is deciding what to hand to an agent, what to write yourself, and what context the agent needs to get it right the first time. 

You ask what a planner is trying to do before you read what the ticket says. You automate the parts of your own process that don't need a human. 

Year one, in order 

First, ship. Deliver features in scheduling and time tracking. Start small, then take one full feature from the product conversation through to release. 

Then, own an area. Pick up a product surface end to end and become the person the team asks about it, including what it should do next. That covers how AI fits your area, which patterns you document for the agent and which calls you keep for yourself. 

Along the way, make what you build safe to change. Restructure and test the paths you build on while you build on them. Extend test coverage where it's lacking. We move fast and keep quality up by automating what a human doesn't need to do, including the checks that catch what an agent got wrong. 

What you'll do 

- Design and build frontend features starting from rough product ideas 

- Deliver features with Claude Code, from the prompt through to the pull request, and review the output as closely as a colleague's 

- Write the patterns, conventions and project context our agents work from, so generated frontend code lands in the right shape 

- Turn tangled domain rules into screens people can use without a manual 

- Fix bugs in your own features and in code you've never seen 

- Improve the code you touch while you touch it, so the next feature in that area costs less 

- Write and maintain automated tests in Jest and Playwright 

- Ship in short cycles with your product team 

- Pair, review, and teach what you know 

How we work 

Frontend in Angular, backend in PHP, a web app and a mobile app in React Native. Tests in Jest and Playwright. We develop AI-assisted with Claude Code as the primary tool, and a growing share of our code starts there. Human review and engineers owning what they ship keep it safe. We ship in short cycles in product teams with mixed specialisations. We pair often, with each other and with an agent open. Every quarter you get time to build and ship one of your own ideas, and we run hackathons. 

Must-haves 

3+ years of professional experience with an SPA framework, Angular preferred. Depth in React or Vue works if you can show you'll carry it over. 

You ship. You've delivered features to real users at a steady pace, and you can tell us what you cut to get them out. 

You've shipped production code with an AI agent. Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot or similar. Tell us where you let it run, where you took the keyboard back, and what you changed about your own workflow after a month of it. 

You automate your tests. Jest and Playwright, or equivalents, and you have an opinion about what deserves a test. 

You simplify. Hand you a tangled domain problem and you produce a screen that hides the tangle. 

You explain your choices. In review, in a design discussion, and to a product manager who doesn't read code. 

You work as a peer. You pair, you review, and you make the people around you better without needing a title to be heard. 

Nice-to-haves 

- Claude Code in particular, or agent setups you've tuned for a team rather than yourself 

- TypeScript at depth 

- Storybook or component library ownership 

- React 

- TDD 

- PHP, or enough backend to reason about the API you're consuming 

- Familiarity with a complex, regulated domain (ours covers scheduling, time tracking, leave, and labour law across countries) 

This might be your dream job if… 

✅ You want your work in front of customers within days 

✅ You'd rather own a feature end to end than take a finished spec 

✅ You want a say in how a team writes frontend code with agents while the answer is still open 

✅ You improve the code you touch without being asked, and you stop before it turns into a six-week rewrite 

✅ You like a domain that takes months to learn 

This probably isn't your dream job if… 

⛔️ You want the technical approach decided before the ticket reaches you 

⛔️ You want a job where AI stays out of your editor 

⛔️ You'd merge agent output you can't explain in review 

⛔️ You'd stop shipping to finish a refactor 

⛔️ You prefer pixel work and would rather leave tests and architecture to someone else 

⛔️ You'd rather work alone than pair and review

- 32 or 40 hours workweek 

- Hybrid, from home or the Zoetermeer office 

- 25 vacation days based on a 40-hour contract 

- Pension plan 

- NS business card or travel expenses reimbursed. 

- Training budget for personal development 

Please be aware that this is not a remote position and we are not taking applications in consideration outside of the Netherlands for this position.

We're currently on an exciting growth journey, scaling rapidly as demand for reliable, high-performance web scraping and data keeps rising.

Profile Overview

This is the hard end of web scraping. The sites we rely on, Google, Amazon, Walmart and many others, actively work to block us, and they change the rules without warning. We're looking for a senior engineer who can go deep on why we're being blocked, work out how the detection actually functions, and design repeatable ways around it. You'll be joining a self-driven, high-autonomy team to take on our most involved problems, with the room and the trust to build something from close to a blank page: an environment that turns one-off breakthroughs into a methodical, repeatable way of defeating anti-bot systems. If you like confronting problems that genuinely resist you, and you work methodically rather than by trial and error, this is an unusually open brief.

Your immediate impact in the first 3-6 months will be:

- Getting a full local environment running and becoming fluent in our systems and how they operate, in the first few weeks.

- Contributing to a proposal on the design for a repeatable environment we can pose anti-bot problems to and get reliable analysis out of.

- Building that environment out over the following months so that, by month six, we can point it at a target or provider and have it reliably tell us how we're being blocked and what is and isn't being used against us.

Your responsibilities

- Analyse how specific anti-bot and bot-mitigation systems (the likes of DataDome, Cloudflare Turnstile, Kasada, PerimeterX and Akamai) detect and block us, and design systems to work around them.

- Turn isolated breakthroughs into durable, repeatable processes: hypothesis, test, discard what's wrong, move on.

- In collaboration with other senior team members, design and build a greenfield agentic environment that can propose and run tests on anti-bot behaviour and bypass approaches, and do it in a way that's well understood and repeatable.

- Work largely independently on deep, concentrated problems, while actively pulling in knowledge from across the wider engineering team.

- Communicate clearly what you plan to do, and step into major incidents when the team needs your depth.

What you bring to the table

- Deep, genuine understanding of how the internet works underneath: HTTP, TLS and fingerprinting, proxies, headers, cookies, and browser behaviour. This is the core of the role and it isn't something we can shortcut.

- Excellent problem-solving built on a scientific, methodical approach: you form a hypothesis, design a test, read the result honestly, and iterate. Trying things at random is the opposite of what this role needs.

- Strong hands-on skills in our stack, Node.js and TypeScript with solid Python, and comfort across backend systems at scale (Postgres, Redis/Valkey, MongoDB, Puppeteer/Camoufox, Kubernetes).

- Real skill at directing AI coding agents with precision, and the judgement to tell strong output from weak. The specific tool doesn't matter (Claude, Codex or similar); knowing how to steer it well is what counts.

- A background that has given you this kind of depth and rigour. That might be scraping, anti-bot or web-security work, reverse engineering, or a research or academic path where you built your own tooling and lived by the scientific method. Direct scraping experience is a strong plus rather than a strict requirement.

- Independence and strong communication: you're comfortable owning hard problems in a remote-first team with little hand-holding, and you keep the team in the loop on your thinking as you go.

What's in it for you

- Ultimate flexibility: We're 100% remote. You can work from wherever you like, whenever you like.

- Freedom and autonomy: We're a high-trust team, and you'll be given lots of flexibility to solve problems in your own way, with plenty of help from the team when you need it.

Think of us as the driving catalyst behind your favorite software success stories. saas.group, established in 2017, is on a mission to turbocharge promising B2B SaaS ventures, unlocking their full potential. As a Software-as-a-Service portfolio powerhouse, we specialize in acquiring small software treasures and polishing them into industry stars. With a dynamic, fully remote team of nearly 400 colleagues spanning 50+ countries we are truly global and we are rewriting the playbook on SaaS innovation and collaboration. Overview 

We are looking for an exceptional full-stack software engineer who will act as a Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) to serve as the critical interface between the central AI Application Modernization Factory and our application teams. The FDE will be temporarily embedded within delivery teams to directly drive the modernization of key applications, ensuring technical success, accelerated adoption of AI-assisted SDLC practices , and lasting upskilling of team members. This is a high-impact, hybrid role requiring advanced software engineering skills, deep knowledge of cloud-native patterns, and proven expertise in consultation, change management, and building strong rapport with diverse teams.

Key Responsibilities 

- Application Modernization Execution: Embed with application teams to provide hands-on technical leadership, driving the design, development, and delivery of modernization efforts (re-platforming, microservices adoption) to AWS cloud-native architectures.

- AI-First SDLC Adoption & Upskilling: Act as the subject matter expert on the AI Modernization Factory's tools and processes (e.g., Cursor, Claude Code). Drive the adoption and change management necessary to embed AI-assisted software development practices into the team’s daily workflow.

- Consultative Engineering & Change Management: Build trust and rapport with new, diverse teams quickly. Identify team-specific technical and process bottlenecks, recommending and implementing solutions, and effectively managing the people/process side of technical change.

- Hands-on Software Development: Make significant code contributions, focusing on setting up architectural scaffolding, CI/CD pipelines, IaC (Terraform), and solving complex, blocking integration challenges for the embedded team.

- Feedback Loop: Serve as the primary feedback channel, relaying practical challenges, tool deficiencies, and necessary process adjustments back to the central Principal Engineer and Architect to continuously improve the factory's capabilities.

- Standards & Quality: Ensure embedded teams adhere to the central factory's engineering standards, including Twelve-Factor App principles, DevSecOps practices, and high-quality coding standards.

Required Qualifications & Experience 

- Experience: 5+ years of progressive experience in Software Engineering, with a focus on enterprise applications and application modernization.

- Full Stack Proficiency: Strong hands-on experience across the full application stack (front-end, back-end, database, infrastructure). Expert proficiency in one or more modern technology languages (e.g., Python, TypeScript, C#, Java).

- Cloud Native & IaC: Deep practical experience building and deploying scalable applications on AWS. Strong proficiency with Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC), specifically Terraform.

- Consulting & Change Management: Proven ability to onboard rapidly, assess team dynamics and technical landscapes, influence technical direction without formal authority, and drive organizational/process change within established engineering teams.

- DevSecOps & CI/CD: Hands-on mastery of setting up and optimizing CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI) and integrating DevSecOps best practices.

- Architectural Understanding: Solid understanding of modern architectural patterns (microservices, serverless, event-driven architecture) and the principles of Domain-Driven Design (DDD).

- Communication & Interpersonal Skills: Exceptional communication, presentation, and listening skills. Ability to articulate complex technical issues and solutions to both technical and non-technical stakeholders effectively.

Preferred Skills (A Plus) 

- Prior experience in a consulting, Staff Engineer, or Forward Deployed role, specifically focused on technical adoption or modernization.

- Direct experience training or mentoring other software engineers in new technologies or methodologies.

- Hands-on experience with modern UI frameworks like React, NextJS, or similar.

- Experience utilizing AI-assisted coding tools (Cursor, Claude Code) in a professional development environment.

- Familiarity with containerization (Docker/Kubernetes) and serverless architectures (AWS Lambda).

Banyan Software may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to assist in screening and/or assessing applicants during the recruitment process. All hiring decisions are made by our team. - Rebuilt our Ops QA admin system from the ground up, replacing an off-the-shelf tool with something tailored to our needs

- Deployed a pipeline to summarise customer calls into concise notes using LLMs, automatically surfaced in ops admin panels — removing the need for manual note-writing

- More than doubled the number of complaints processed by agents through a combination of targeted AI automation and improved UX

We’d consider the following essential to the role:

- You have 8+ years of professional experience as a software engineer

- Solid experience with Python in a web application context. You have some experience with web frameworks like FastAPI, Django or Flask. We use FastAPI.

- Experience with Javascript/Typescript and a modern JS framework such as React, Angular or Vue.js. We generally use React & NextJS. You can build a frontend that's good enough for internal tooling

- A keen desire to want to learn and input into a highly collaborative team

- Exposure to Domain Driven Design, Message-Driven Systems and Event Sourcing

- Experience with cloud infrastructure, particularly AWS

- SQL, and finding your way around data schemas

- Shipping containerised software with Argo, Kubernetes, Docker and Terraform

- Technical Interview

title: Senior Full Stack
description:
Headquarters: Tallinn, Estonia

URL: https://toggl.com/jobs/ 

We are looking for a Senior Full Stack Engineer to join one of our Product Tribes, the cross-functional units that own the end-to-end experience for a specific Toggl user role. You'll join the Tribe building for managers, the people who plan work, protect margins, and keep projects on time and on budget.

You own significant parts of that experience end-to-end, working hands-on with product and design to ship work that matters. You'll do this as we build and launch Toggl 2.0, our consolidated planning, time tracking, and time intelligence product.

The salary for this position is €83,000 annually. 

You can work from anywhere in the world as long as your main location is between UTC-4 and UTC+4. 

The Role 

As a Senior Full Stack Engineer, you own meaningful parts of the product end-to-end, from the data model and the API to the interface someone actually clicks: the technical approach, the quality of what ships, and whether it actually works for the people using it. You are accountable not for tickets closed, but for clarity, craft, and outcomes.

You'll work in the Tribe serving managers, across planning and capacity management, dashboards, and billable work. This is some of the most data-dense, interaction-heavy surface area in the product: schedules and capacity views, reports, and visualizations that have to stay fast and readable at real customer scale. The interesting problems live on both sides of the API here - the query behind a capacity view matters as much as how that view renders. You'll build with React and TypeScript on the frontend and our backend services (mostly Golang) and data layer (Postgres) behind them, alongside a product manager, a designer, and engineers who are used to owning their work and pushing back when something isn't right. In a tribe of 5 other engineers, your impact and visibility are high.

Our team meetings are scheduled between 11:00 and 16:00 UTC. Your availability and commitment to participate in these sessions are essential for effective collaboration and team alignment.

Your main responsibilities will be:

Ownership and delivery 

- 
Take projects from problem to production. Own the technical approach for major features front to back, break the work down sensibly, sequence it, and ship in slices rather than one big drop.

- 
Make the technical calls in your area. Choose between options, name the tradeoffs, and decide without waiting for permission or escalating routine judgment.

- 
Keep your work visible without being chased. Flag risks and slips early, keep the Tribe in the loop, and unblock yourself.

Craft and quality across the stack 

- 
Build interfaces people trust with dense, real-world data. Planning views, dashboards, and reports that stay fast, accessible, and readable when the dataset gets ugly.

- 
Design the data and API layer those views depend on. Model it so the feature you're building now doesn't make the next three harder.

- 
Own performance as a feature, end to end. Profile, measure, and fix the slow query and the slow render instead of hoping the data stays small.

- 
Write code others can work in. Sensible components and services, real test coverage where it earns its keep, and a codebase that's easier to change after you touch it.

Working with product and design 

- 
Shape solutions, don't just implement them. Push on the problem, question requirements that don't hold up, and propose simpler paths when you see one.

- 
Partner closely with design. Prototype early, spot the edge cases in a flow before it's built, and hold the bar on UX quality with your designer rather than after handoff.

- 
Stay close to users and evidence. Join user tests, read the feedback, look at the data, and let it change what you build.

Raising the bar 

- 
Review code with intent. Give precise, actionable feedback that makes the change and the person better.

- 
Mentor and interview. Help other engineers grow, and help us hire well.

- 
Improve things across team boundaries. Spot shared components and duplicated work between Tribes, and raise it before we build the same thing twice.

AI as core leverage 

- 
Use AI tools extensively in your daily work for exploration, prototyping, code generation and review, debugging, research, and writing. AI fluency is not optional. It's part of how you increase your speed, depth, and impact - and you're expected to help the rest of the Tribe get better at it too.

About You 

You will thrive in this role if you:

- 
Have significant experience building and shipping production web applications end to end, and can lead major projects rather than just contribute to them.

- 
Are genuinely comfortable on both sides of the stack. You're deep on one side and properly capable on the other, not someone who hands off at the API boundary.

- 
Have deep, practical knowledge of JavaScript, TypeScript, React, and modern CSS - including state management and side-effect handling in large applications.

- 
Are solid on backend fundamentals: at least one backend language you know well, API design, relational data modelling, and enough instinct for query performance to spot the problem before production does. Prior Golang experience is not mandatory but you have to be willing to adopt it and become comfortable with it fast. 

- 
Hold an extremely high bar for quality. You know what great looks like, you notice the details others miss, and you don't ship work you wouldn't put your name on.

- 
Have a knack for data-heavy product surfaces - performance, readability, and the principles behind a chart that actually communicates something.

- 
Care about the user's problem, not just the ticket. You start from what someone is trying to get done and work back to the implementation.

- 
Own outcomes, not output. You follow your work into production, watch how it behaves, and fix what needs fixing.

- 
Thrive in ambiguity and move fast. You make confident decisions with incomplete information, adapt when things change, and course-correct without drama.

- 
Are hands-on with AI tools. You actively use AI as a core part of how you build, not a side experiment, and you have opinions about where it helps and where it doesn't.

- 
Don't need to be managed. You set your own direction, keep people in the loop, and ask for help when it matters.

- 
Have excellent written and verbal English communication skills. You write clearly, explain technical tradeoffs to non-engineers without jargon, and default to async communication that others can follow.

- 
Are eager to contribute to the engineering team's growth - code review, mentoring, and interviewing included.

- 
Value transparency, ownership, and speed over perfection. You ship, learn, and improve rather than waiting for the perfect plan.

- 
Nice to have: 

- 
Experience with TanStack is a bonus, and so is a real understanding of frontend caching and eventual consistency, we'd love to hire someone who's dealt with that tradeoff directly.

- 
Experience with capacity planning, scheduling, reporting, or other complex B2B SaaS products.

- 
Experience working with distributed or microservice systems, a basic understanding of infrastructure and infrastructure as code, and some experience creating, improving, or debugging CI/CD pipelines.

This Role Is NOT 

- 
A ticket-taker role. If you want fully specced work handed to you, this isn't the right fit.

- 
A pixel-pusher translating finished designs into code with no say in the problem or the solution.

- 
A role where you hand off at the API boundary. If "that's a backend ticket" is your instinct, this will frustrate you.

- 
A role where quality is someone else's job. Toggl doesn't have a dedicated QA
team or layer: there's no separate team that will catch your bugs, write your
tests, or own your performance regressions.

- 
A place to work in isolation from users. You'll be expected to know who you're building for and why.

- 
A role for people who need heavy process, frequent approvals, or top-down direction to do their best work.

The Team 

We are a global team of ~80 awesome people working from over 40 countries around the globe. We hire globally, you work locally—in the heart of London, a beach outside of Río de Janeiro, or a quiet village near Florence, the choice is yours. Every few months we travel to meet up somewhere in the world and spend some quality time together. We place a huge amount of trust in our people, and we measure the outcomes rather than the work itself. Our values fuel our results.

What's Happening at Toggl 

Toggl is at an exciting turning point. We're taking our best-in-class time tracking - trusted and loved by millions of users worldwide - and expanding it into something bigger: Toggl 2.0 . One product that brings together time tracking, planning, capacity management, reporting, and insight. The idea is simple: better time tracking creates better data, which powers everything else. We call it time intelligence. We build with AI throughout, and we think it's a real multiplier for strong engineers rather than a substitute for them. The judgment, the tradeoffs, and the accountability for what ships stay with people.

Benefits 

- 
Freedom to choose when and how much you work—we only measure results

- 
24 days of paid time off a year, plus your local holidays

- 
Unlimited sick leave

- 
In-person meetups for team-building (expenses covered)

- 
4-6 weeks paid sabbatical (depending on tenure)

- 
Laptop budget up to 2,500€ and it renews every 3 years

- 
€2,000 budget to set up your home office and an additional €300 every year after 3 years of tenure

- 
€3,000 per year for co-working space membership and/or internet service at home

- 
€4,000 per year contribution to use for training, workshops, and conferences

- 
€2,400 per year contribution for any equipment or services to improve and/or maintain your physical and mental health

- 
Support for buying tools you need for doing your best work (even eyeglasses if you need a new pair)

title: Lead Software Engineer
description:
Building the intelligence behind Solskin

Are you a driven person who wants to make buildings come alive?

We are Zurich Soft Robotics (ZSR), a Zurich-based startup developing Solskin – a climate-adaptive solar facade. Solskin is not just a PV system or a shading system; it’s an intelligent skin that uses weather and building data, occupant feedback, and AI algorithms to decide how the facade moves, so buildings stay comfortable, avoid overheating, and use energy as efficiently as possible. Solskin is already running on several buildings across Switzerland, with many more to follow.

In this role, you own the software that makes that happen. You write the code that runs Solskin, keep it reliable in the field, and constantly improve it. You will also architect and lead our future sensor-to-data platform. Your focus is where software meets hardware, and the control and AI on top of it. You don't need to be a front-end specialist.

What you will do

This is a hands-on leadership position: you code every day.

Own the full stack: You maintain and develop the whole software stack, from cloud and data management to user-facing applications, and from low-level embedded firmware to high-level AI controllers learning from users. You keep it reliable and keep making it better.

Be the link between the teams: You build the software that runs on real buildings and support the hardware team. You also build the internal tools used by sales and the business team. 

Lead what comes next : With the CEO and CTO, you set the software direction and lead development of future products. 

Our stack: 

- Backend: Python, FastAPI, PyTorch

- Frontend: React, TypeScript

- Hardware: C/C++, STM32 microcontrollers, Beckhoff PLCs

- Database: PostgreSQL (TimescaleDB)

- DevOps & Cloud: Linux, Docker, AWS, Grafana

What we are looking for

Required: 

- Education : MSc or PhD in Computer Science, Robotics, Electrical or Mechanical Engineering, or similar.

- Python : This is a must. You write clean Python that runs in production, on real systems.

- Embedded & Hardware: Shipped C/C++ on microcontrollers running on physical hardware; comfortable working with sensors, actuators, and basic electronics. 

- Applied AI & Control: Understanding of modern control and ML/RL methods, with hands-on PyTorch experience applied to physical or dynamic systems.

- Cloud & data : You are comfortable with PostgreSQL, Docker and AWS.

- Leadership attitude : You take ownership, make decisions, and want to grow as a leader.

- Languages : English. German is a big plus.

- Hybrid setting : You will be expected to be on-site at least three days per week, and sometimes at customers’ locations, to work on real products.

- Availability : 100%, as soon as possible.

- Work-permit: You need the right to work in Switzerland for this position.

Preferred: 

- Startup experience: You have worked in a startup before and know what that means.

- Building modeling and control: You have prior experience handling building data, modeling building dynamics, and developing building controllers; ideally with ML and RL tools. 

- Frontend: React and TypeScript.

Mindset: 

- Hands-on: You lead, and you still do the hard work yourself.

- Fast: You are pragmatic and iterate quickly. Things break, and plans change, and that doesn't scare you.

- Purpose: You care about climate and want to make buildings smarter.

Benefits

Impact: Your code runs on real buildings. You see the result of your work.

Ownership: A key role with a real say in our product and technology, and room to grow with the company.

Flexibility: Hybrid work and flexible hours. We like being in the Zurich office together, so plan for regular office days.

Team: A small, skilled, and down-to-earth team that helps each other out.

The reality: We are a startup. It is often messy; things rarely work the first time, and the workload is real. In return, you get a lot of freedom and responsibility from day one.

Sounds like you?

Send us your CV and a short document instead of a classic cover letter. It doesn’t need to be long, just enough for us to understand who you are and where you stand. Please cover these points:

- About you: A short description of yourself.

- Proud of: One thing you are really proud of, in a few sentences.

- Startup: Why do you fit a startup?

- Software meets hardware: Your experience where software and hardware come together.

- Juggeling many hats: You’ll rarely finish one thing from A to Z without interruptions: different stacks, different people, different projects, and on-site surprises. Describe a time your work was like that, and how you handled it.

title: Lead Frontend / Fullstack Engineer
description:
Über Protofy

Wir sind Protofy, die Outcome Agency aus Hamburg, und entwickeln seit über 10 Jahren digitale Produkte, Plattformen und KI-Systeme, die messbar wirken. Technologie ist für uns kein Selbstzweck, sondern ein Business Case, den wir in Umsatz, Effizienz und Wachstum übersetzen.

Deine Rolle

Als technische*r Lead führst Du engagierte Teams und sorgst dafür, dass auch komplexe Projekte pragmatisch, sorgfältig und wirtschaftlich umgesetzt werden. Wir entwickeln Websites und Mobile-Apps für Branchen wie E-Commerce, Wissensmanagement und Sport. Unsere Projekte laufen drei bis neun Monate oder werden als Produkte langfristig weiterentwickelt. Du bringst fundierte Erfahrung mit React sowie in Node.js, Flutter oder Kotlin mit und hast ein sehr gutes Verständnis von Architektur.

Den Entscheider*innen unserer Kund*innen begegnest Du auf Augenhöhe: Du leitest Architekturworkshops eigenständig und unterstützt uns bei Pitches. Gemeinsam mit Deinen Kolleg*innen aus Produkt Designer*innen und Product Owner*innen verantwortest Du Spezifikation, Umsetzung, Testing und Deployment von Features.

Neue Technologien erschließt Du hands-on und machst sie für das Team nutzbar. Außerdem gestaltest Du professionelle Standards in der gesamten Organisation mit, insbesondere für KI-gestützte Entwicklung. Den Großteil Deiner Zeit arbeitest Du selbst im Code, daneben übernimmst Du Führung, Kundenkontakt und Themen der Organisation.

Deine typische Woche

- Du bist technischer Ansprechpartner*in für die Entscheider*innen unserer Kund*innen und berätst sie strategisch

- Du unterstützt Pitches, erarbeitest Slides und technische Konzepte und präsentierst sie

- Du führst Projekte technisch ganzheitlich, von der Architektur bis zum Deployment

- Du entwirfst neue Funktionen mit Produktmanager*innen und UX-Designer*innen und setzt sie gemeinsam mit Deinem Team um

- Du baust neue Themen und Technologien hands-on im Projekt auf, z. B. neue Shopsysteme, Frameworks oder Cloud-Provider

- Du begleitest Dein Team, gibst regelmäßig Feedback und förderst Deine Kolleg*innen durch Tech-Mentoring

- Du gestaltest Entwicklungsprozesse pragmatisch mit, insbesondere KI-gestützte Entwicklung (Tools, Workflows, Qualitätssicherung)

- Du behältst die Wirtschaftlichkeit im Blick: Du schätzt Aufwände, achtest auf Budgets und unterstützt das Projektmanagement

- Du entwickelst die gesamte Organisation aktiv mit

Das bringst du mit

- Du hast 7+ Jahre Erfahrung in der Web- oder App-Entwicklung

- Du hast 4+ Jahre Erfahrung als Tech Lead bzw. in der technischen Führung von Teams

- Du hast fundierte Erfahrung mit React sowie in Node.js, Flutter oder Kotlin

- Du hast mehrjährige Erfahrung in der technischen Verantwortung mittelgroßer Projekte (500+ Personentage)

- Du hast Erfahrung mit Application Architecture und begleitest Teams dabei, Anwendungen auf der grünen Wiese aufzusetzen

- Du kannst Projekte ganzheitlich technisch führen

- Du behältst auch in intensiven Projektphasen einen klaren Kopf und gehst gelassen mit Unsicherheit um

- Du übernimmst gern Verantwortung über Deine eigene Arbeit hinaus und lernst gern Neues

- Du sprichst verhandlungssicher Deutsch und Englisch

Deine ersten Monate bei Protofy

In deinen ersten Wochen wirst du dich in unsere bestehenden Projekte und Architekturkonzepte einarbeiten und erste Features für unsere Kund*innen umsetzen. Du tauschst dich eng mit dem Team aus und übernimmst schrittweise die Verantwortung für die technische Ausrichtung von Web-Anwendungen. Wenn du nicht alle Anforderungen auf Anhieb erfüllst, aber das nötige Fundament mitbringst, freuen wir uns trotzdem auf deine Bewerbung.

title: Software Engineer, Web (Growth)
description:
We are looking for someone to join us as an early member of the Web team, owning the user-facing web at amo. For many people, the web is where they first meet our apps: a link shared by a friend, opened in a messenger or a social feed, often seconds before they decide whether to download. That moment matters a lot to us.

In the initial months, you’ll work closely with the team on the surfaces that bring new people into our products, gradually taking ownership of a growing part of our consumer web experience. Given our stage, we’re seeking versatile engineers comfortable working across product, engineering and growth.

We value team members who delve deep into their respective domains, aiming to cultivate a team of subject matter experts with a high sense of ownership. This commitment to expertise is an expectation for every team member.

As a Web Engineer, your day-to-day will include: 

Consumer Web Experiences 

Building fast, beautiful, conversion-focused web experiences that show off our apps at their best, from the first link someone taps to the moment they open the app. You’ll turn designs into polished UI that loads instantly on any device and in any in-app browser, and you’ll care about every millisecond and every pixel.

Deep Linking & App Entry 

Owning the bridge between web and app: Universal Links, App Links, deferred deep linking, attribution, and App Clips. Whether the user already has the app or not, every link should take them exactly where they expect to go.

Sharing & Rich Previews 

Making everything shared from our apps look great everywhere it lands. That includes generating dynamic OG metadata and preview images at scale, and iterating on what gets shared and how it’s presented, based on what actually converts.

Analytics & Experimentation 

Designing and maintaining our event tracking taxonomy (Amplitude) so that the data is consistent, well organized and trusted across teams. You’ll instrument funnels end-to-end, run rigorous A/B tests, and turn the results into decisions.

Growth Initiatives 

Identifying and shipping new ways to improve acquisition and conversion. We expect you to look at the funnel, form your own hypotheses, build, measure, and then either scale or drop the idea. You’ll be an active contributor to the roadmap, not just its executor.

Owning your scope 

You’ll be responsible for the architecture, performance, monitoring and reliability of everything you ship. We value engineers who take full ownership of their scope, and who proactively address issues before anyone asks.

Your Skills & Experience: 

We are hiring multiple engineers of varying levels, so please indicate your years of experience on the application form to apply for the appropriate position.

- 5+ years of professional experience building consumer-facing web products.

- Deep expertise in React / Next.js, TypeScript and Node.js.

- Strong understanding of web performance: rendering strategies (SSR, edge, static), caching, CDNs, Core Web Vitals, and how mobile and in-app browsers behave.

- Hands-on experience with deep linking, Universal Links / App Links and attribution. Experience with App Clips is a big plus.

- Experience designing analytics taxonomies and running experiments, and real care for data quality.

- A growth mindset: you think in funnels and conversion rates, and you love moving a metric.

- Strong product and visual taste. You notice the 2px misalignment and the 100ms delay.

- Comfortable working autonomously across frontend and backend. Knowledge of infrastructure (Bazel, GCP, Kubernetes) is a plus.

- Passion and experience building consumer-facing products. We’d love to hear about things you’ve shipped!

AI as a multiplier 

AI is part of how we build every day. We’re looking for engineers with a real grasp of these tools, who use them to multiply their output and not to make up for missing expertise. You should be able to drive an agent through a complex change, judge what it produces, spot where it’s subtly wrong, and stand behind every line that ships.

The bar 

We’re looking for exceptional engineers, and we set the bar high on purpose. In return, you’ll get real ownership of a high-impact surface, products used by millions of people, a team that ships in days rather than quarters, a modern stack with top-tier tooling, and colleagues who will push you to grow.

You don’t need to speak French to apply (and you don’t need perfect English; we’ll help you ramp up quickly).

Life at amo 

To ensure that everyone is set up for success within our way of working, we work together onsite 5 days a week.

We wanted to make sure coming to the office was as comfortable as possible for you:

- We chose a location in central Paris, near Opera (Metro lines 3,8,9 and RER A).

- We have a beautiful Parisian-style office with high ceilings, balconies, and huge windows. So a lot of natural light!

Because life outside of work should also be stress-free, we cover:

- Health care (100% coverage).

- Maternity Leave, Paternity Leave, Second Parent Leave (salary maintained at 100%).

- Vacation days: 8-9 weeks (total) per year - (European summer? 🥹😎).

- 5 weeks of paid time off (by the state);

- 1-2 additional weeks (RTT, based on our company contract);

- ~11 bank holidays.

We shut down entirely twice a year, two weeks in summer and one week in winter to allow everyone to truly recharge and to avoid prolonged slowdowns (especially in the summer). These pauses are part of your total vacation time, giving everyone a real chance to unplug and recharge. No Slack, no email, no FOMO.

Relocation 

- We love the diverse perspectives we get from having people from all over the world join us (68% of our team is international), and so we of course support relocation to Paris with:

- Help and sponsored visa process.

- 1 month of Airbnb 100% covered by amo upon arrival.

- Assistance from a trusted relocation agency to find your permanent home.

- Help with french paperwork like opening a french social security account, tax forms, getting your carte vitale (free healthcare) and more.

- French lessons to be fully set with your new Parisian life.

description:
Join our mission, join Doctolib! 

We are looking for a Senior AI Engineer to join the Patient team in Paris. 

The Patient domain sits at the heart of Doctolib's mission: ensuring everyone has better access to the care they need, receives better care from health professionals, and can actively prevent health problems to improve their wellbeing.

You’ll design the search and recommendation engines behind our health companion, helping 100M patients across Europe instantly navigate to the exact care they need while delivering trusted, curated insights at every step. The retrieval and recommendation architecture you own will directly shape how relevant, fast, and trustworthy that experience is for every one of them.

Your responsibilities include but are not limited to:

- Design and build the production search & recommendation architecture: full retrieval, ranking, reranking pipeline with standard and off-the-shelf components (vector search, semantic retrieval, LLM/managed rerankers).

- Establish strong baselines first (prompts, RAG, model selection) before reaching for custom ML.

- Build evaluation and observability into every stage, with offline and online evaluation.

- Set up the data/event feedback loops that drive iteration and feed deeper ML later.

- Improve search relevance and ranking on Patient facing products , raising result quality

- Own production quality: latency reliability, monitoring, and maintainability.

- Partner with ML Engineers and collaborate closely with PMs and SWEs to define, build, and ship AI-powered features that deliver measurable value to users and the business. 

Who you are 

Before you read on: if you don't have the exact profile described below, but you feel this job description matches your skill set, we still encourage you to apply. 

You could be our next team mate if you have:

- Production deployment : ability to ship algorithms to production (ECS-based service on AWS)

- Strong analytical mindset: r esult-oriented, patient-first approach

- Significant experience as a Software or/and AI engineer shipping search or recommendation systems to production. 

- Hands-on experience building end-to-end retrieval: ranking, reranking pipelines and familiar with nDCG, MAP, Recall@k, MRR

- AI-engineering proficiency : turning foundation models and off-the-shelf components into production systems: embeddings & vector search, semantic retrieval, RAG, LLM-based or managed rerankers (e.g. Vertex AI). You can succeed without training a model from scratch

- Evaluation & observability built into every stage (retrieval, ranker, reranker) — offline and online eval, A/B testing, position-bias handling, monitoring

- Production deployment — ability to ship reliable, low-latency services to production (hundreds-of-ms SLAs), with care for data quality and long-term maintainability

Now, it would be fantastic if you:

- Experience at a B2C marketplace (e-commerce, hospitality, travel)

- Additional ML methodologies: pattern mining, recommendation systems, experimentation, or causal inference 

- Have experience with search engines or information retrieval concepts

- Have exposure to learning-to-rank or feature engineering (for breaking ceilings later, alongside ML Engineers)

- Have experience in a healthcare or other regulated domain (GDPR / HDS)

- Our solutions are built on a single, fully cloud-native platform that supports web and mobile app interfaces, multiple languages, and is adapted to country and healthcare specialty requirements.

title: Full Stack Engineer
description:
Who We Are 

Our mission is to make the world programmable. Sight is one of the key ways we understand the world, and soon this will be true for the software we use, too.

We’re building the tools, community, and resources needed to make the world programmable with artificial intelligence. Roboflow simplifies building and using computer vision models. Today, over 1M+ developers, including those from half the Fortune 100, use Roboflow’s machine learning open source and hosted tools. That includes counting cells to accelerate cancer research, improving construction site safety , digitizing floor plans , preserving coral reef populations , guiding drone flight , and much more .

Roboflow is supported by great customers and investors, having raised over 63 million from Y Combinator, Google Ventures, Craft Ventures, Sam Altman, Lachy Groom, amongst other leading software investors.

Roboflowers are passionate builders who value ownership, accountability, and a bias toward action. We're curious, hands-on with new tech, and prefer showing our work over talking about it. Many of us have a founder mindset and thrive in our high-autonomy environment.

What You'll Do 

You'll be tasked with a wide range of projects. Each engineer has a realm they focus on, but we're still small enough that we don't have the luxury of deep specialization. We're looking for technical generalists that aren’t afraid to dive into a new stack or toolchain if the need arises (but JavaScript and Node.js make up the brunt of the existing codebase).

Most of the things we work on are parts of the core product (which is an end-to-end pipeline for building computer vision projects spanning from image ingestion to annotation to training and deployment) but from time to time we're also working on things like integrating marketing and sales tools, fighting fires, automating internal processes, and open source projects.

You'll have a wide degree of freedom to advocate for which projects you think should be highest priority and will contribute to our strategy decisions. If you need a rigid list of tasks spelled out in a multi-month roadmap, this role probably won't be a good fit.

The majority of our codebase is written in JavaScript, our machine learning and image processing pipeline is in Python. We run primarily on Firebase and GCS, with some machine learning infrastructure on AWS. We're increasingly using Docker (both internally and for customer facing products like our edge inference server). A lot of our code runs in the browser (including some Tensorflow JS) but we're also working on building APIs and client libraries in several languages.

You certainly don't need to be experienced in all of these areas; but should be excited to learn new skill sets as you need them. We also hope you'll bring some new knowledge and experiences you can share to help level-up the rest of the team.

We’re especially keen to add some rigor to our processes and build the foundation for rapidly scaling the engineering organization (for example: we currently have limited tests and are not using an opinionated front-end framework -- things that will need to change over the coming months in order to be able to seamlessly expand the team).

Example Projects 

- 
Creating a filtering interface so our users can mix and match their images based on metadata like the time of day they were captured, the GPS location, or custom tags they've applied.

- 
Expanding our annotation tool to support new functionality (like polygonal annotations image segmentation).

- 
Integrating the core app with external APIs for things like outsourcing annotation tasks and analyzing deployed model performance.

- 
Streamlining our onboarding flow.

- 
Deeper integrations with our other products like Roboflow Universe and our REST API.

- 
Next-generation model assisted labeling.

- 
Optimizing speed and scalability.

Who You'll Be Working With 

Our team of ~120 attracts talent like executives that wanted to return to building, founders with a 100M+ exit, Roboflow users turned team members, open source contributors, a cyclist who biked across the United States, prolific high school hackers, a CTO from 100+ engineering organization, amongst many exceptional others.

You will directly be working with our Engineering Lead and a team of Full Stack Engineers.

Where You'll Work 

Roboflow is fully distributed. We currently have Hubs in New York City and San Francisco (and plan to open more as we grow density in new cities). We provide opportunities (like team onsites in different cities) and resources (like a $4000/yr travel stipend) to work in person with other team members as much as you'd like, while also supporting remote team members. You can work from one of our Hubs (we offer a relocation bonus), work from home, work at co-working spaces, etc. We want you to work where you work best!

When You'll Work 

Roboflow primarily operates during the daytime hours in the US and there are some synchronous meetings you’ll be expected to attend each week. Apart from that, we have a flexible schedule that allows you to work collaboratively with other team members and asynchronously when needed.

What You'll Receive 

To determine your salary, we use a number of market and data-driven salary sources. We review all salaries every six months to ensure we stay in line with the market.

The target compensation for this role is $165,000 - $195,000 base.

In addition to our cash compensation, we offer generous perks and benefits. Below are some of the highlights:

- 
$4000/yr Travel Stipend to travel anywhere anytime to work alongside other Roboflowers

- 
$350/mo Productivity stipend to spend on things that make your work environment more productive, like high-speed internet at home or a co-working space

- 
$350/mo AI Tools stipend

- 
$150/mo team lunch stipend

- 
$500/one time home office stipend

- 
Cover up to 100% of your health insurance costs for you and your partner or family

- 
Equity in the company so we are all invested in the future of computer vision

Interview Process (6+ hours) 

Below is the interview process you can expect for this role. We are all motivated to work with an exceptional team and don't currently have in-house recruiters. You will be speaking directly with our team about what it's like to work and thrive at Roboflow. We like to be decisive and work fast, so don't be surprised if all the below conversations happen over a day or two.

Introduction Phase: 

- 
[30m] Meet with hiring manager for introduction to assess overall mindset and skillset.

- 
[60m] Technical assessment with a Roboflow engineer.

Build with Roboflow Phase: 

- 
You will build a small project with Roboflow to showcase your technical and product skills.

Team Interview Phase: 

- 
[45m] Meet with your hiring manager and our CTO to demo your project

Final Interview Stage: 

- 
[45m] Meet with Head of Operations for a culture discussion.

- 
[60m / Optional] Meet with CEO.

Not sure if this is you? 

We want a diverse, global team with a broad range of experience and perspectives. If this job sounds great, but you’re not sure if you qualify, look into our Former Founders role or subscribe to our career newsletter by emailing "Subscribe" to operations@roboflow.com . We carefully consider every application and will either move forward with you, find another team that might be a better fit, keep in touch for future opportunities, or thank you for your time.

Equal Employment Opportunity 

At Roboflow, we believe great ideas come from everywhere—and everyone. We’re proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to building a diverse and inclusive team. We consider all qualified applicants regardless of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, age, veteran status, or any other legally protected characteristics.

About us 

At Trainline, our purpose is to empower greener travel choices, connecting people and places. Trainline enables millions of travellers to find and book the best value tickets across carriers, fares, and journey options through our highly rated mobile app, website, and B2B partner channels. 

Great journeys start with Trainline 🚄 

We’re Europe’s leading independent rail platform, helping millions of travellers find and book the best-value rail and coach journeys across our app, website and partner channels.

Our job is to make the green travel choice the best choice. By building a better train travel experience, we help more people choose rail - creating a positive impact for customers, our business and the planet.

We’re a team of more than 1,000 Trainliners from over 50 nationalities, working across London, Paris, Barcelona, Milan, Edinburgh and Madrid. Now is a brilliant time to join us and help shape the future of travel.

Introducing the Trainline MLOps Team 👋 

Our MLOps team helps machine learning (ML) and AI teams across Trainline build, launch and run their products reliably. As a Senior MLOps Engineer, you will help shape how we operate AI and ML systems, including the infrastructure and tooling behind our internal ML/AI platforms and our customer-facing products. You will work on systems that are already being built and used across Trainline, so your impact will be real and visible. No two weeks look the same: one day you might be building out our ML platform, the next helping shape the architecture of our multi-agent AI products, and the next improving the developer experience with new tooling and standards. This is a hands-on role with technical leadership at its core. You will join an established team, working alongside our MLOps Engineering Manager and a small group of engineers, as we support a growing number of ML and AI teams. There is genuine scope to influence our technical direction, develop our engineering practices and mentor junior colleagues.

In this role as the Senior MLOps Engineer, you will... 🚅 

- Take a leading technical role in helping teams across Trainline adopt and operate ML and AI tooling as the technology evolves

- Support AI infrastructure, working with the teams building our internal platform and customer-facing products, making sure products are well governed, monitored and deployed through automation

- Build and drive adoption of one standard way to deploy ML and AI products, so that new products onboard quickly and reach production faster

- Automate the modernisation of our services across products, including fixing and preventing security vulnerabilities in libraries and dependencies

- Strengthen our MLOps foundations by improving cost tracking, finding ways to reduce costs, addressing security vulnerabilities and standardising engineering practices

- Contribute to technical strategy, evaluating options and making well-reasoned decisions where there is no established approach

- Communicate technical decisions clearly and help prioritise requests from the ML teams we support

- Mentor fellow engineers and share knowledge through documentation and enablement across the organisation

We’d love to hear from you if you have...🔍 

- Hands-on experience with IaC and CI/CD tooling, ideally Terraform and GitHub Actions, though alternatives such as AWS CloudFormation and Jenkins are also relevant

- Experience with containerised workloads using Docker and cloud platforms, ideally AWS, though GCP and Azure will be considered

- Experience productionising AI products, including agentic systems and the AIOps tooling behind them, ideally using AWS Bedrock AgentCore or similar

- Experience with managed or self-hosted ML infrastructure, such as Amazon SageMaker, feature stores (e.g. Feast) and DAG tooling (e.g. Airflow, Metaflow, or similar)

- Experience with model experiment tracking, ideally MLflow or Weights & Biases, and with monitoring tools such as EvidentlyAI, CometML, Grafana or New Relic

- Experience writing production-quality, tested Python code

- Experience leading or contributing significantly to major platform changes and migrations, and the ability to lead technical work through ambiguity

- Clear communication, sound prioritisation, and a track record of getting other teams to adopt shared standards and of mentoring colleagues

Nice to have's... 🔑 

- Knowledge of cloud topics such as networking fundamentals (VPC, security groups, CDN, WAF, etc.) and identity and access management (IAM, EntraID, SSO, etc.)

- Experience with any of our wider tech stack and partners, including Spacelift, Braintrust and ElevenLabs.

More information: 

Enjoy fantastic perks like private healthcare & dental insurance, a generous work from abroad policy, 2-for-1 share purchase plans, an EV Scheme to further reduce carbon emissions, extra festive time off, and excellent family-friendly benefits. 

We prioritise career growth with clear career paths, transparent pay bands, personal learning budgets, and regular learning days. Jump on board and supercharge your career from day one! 

We're operating a hybrid model and ask that Trainliners work from the office a minimum of 60% of their time over a 12-week period. We also have a 28-day Work from Abroad policy.

- 💭 Think Big - We're building the future of rail 

- ✔️ Own It - We focus on every customer, partner and journey 

- 🤝 Travel Together - We're one team 

- ♻️ Do Good - We make a positive impact

description:

We are redefining healthcare by putting the customer first and delivering access to care that is affordable, accessible, and personal, from diagnosis to treatment to delivery. No two people are the same, so we provide access to personalized care designed for results. By normalizing health & wellness challenges and innovating on their solutions, we’re making better health outcomes easier to achieve. 

Hims & Hers is a public company, traded on the NYSE under the ticker symbol “HIMS.” To learn more about the brand and offerings, you can visit hims.com/about and hims.com/how-it-works . For information on the company’s outstanding benefits, culture, and its talent-first flexible/remote work approach, see below and visit www.hims.com/careers-professionals .

About the Role:

We’re looking for a Staff Forward Deployed Engineer who’s passionate about using AI to change how teams across the business get their work done.

You’ll embed with a team, learn how they actually work, and build the AI-powered workflows that make them faster and more effective. You start by mapping how the function operates today, then decide together with the team where AI can create the most value and build it.

This is not a support role, a solutions-engineering role, or staff augmentation. You are a full engineer who works at the boundary between our AI platform and a business domain. You ship production systems, and the best of what you build for one team becomes a reusable capability for the whole company.

You Will:

- 
Embed with a team. Work alongside a function for sustained periods, joining their day-to-day so you understand how they really operate.

- 
Map how the work gets done. Build a clear picture of the function's current workflows and surface where time, handoffs, rework, and manual effort pile up.

- 
Find where AI creates the most value. Prioritize the opportunities that will move the function's outcomes the most, and align with the team on what to tackle.

- 
Build it in production. Ship real, AI-powered workflows that solve the problems you find, working hands-on with the team and our platform.

- 
Scale what works. Turn proven solutions into reusable capabilities so a win with one team accelerates the whole organization.

- 
Own the outcome. Measure success by the business results your partners achieve: revenue generated, cost saved, cycle time reduced, manual work eliminated.

You Have:

- 
8+ years of professional software engineering experience.

- 
Strong hands-on coding skills and experience delivering production systems across complex codebases.

- 
Strong Python, plus backend or fullstack depth in one or more of: Node.js, Kotlin, Java, Go, React, TypeScript, or mobile.

- 
Experience with cloud infrastructure (AWS, Docker, Kubernetes), CI/CD workflows, and SQL.

- 
Working knowledge of LLMs and agentic patterns: prompt engineering, tool use, RAG and retrieval, context management, evaluation and observability, and agent orchestration with frameworks like MCP, LangChain, or similar.

- 
The ability to get productive fast in codebases and domains you have never worked in.

- 
Excellent communication and collaboration skills. You partner across technical and business teams, translate between them, and produce docs and findings that both engineers and non-technical stakeholders can act on.

- 
Nice to have:

- 
Experience extracting structure from unstructured data (transcripts, documents, conversations) with LLMs.

- 
Familiarity with workflow automation tooling (n8n, Zapier, Temporal, or similar).

- 
Familiarity with process mining or workflow analysis (event logs, process discovery, BPMN).

You'll Thrive Here If You:

- 
Love experimenting with AI tools and applying them to real engineering and business challenges.

- 
Enjoy embedding with teams outside engineering and bridging the language gap between technical and business partners.

- 
Treat discovery as engineering work, not a preamble to it.

- 
Enjoy translating early prototypes into production-ready, maintainable systems.

- 
Are curious, pragmatic, and impact-driven. You measure success by the business outcomes your partners achieve.

Competitive salary & equity compensation for full-time roles

- 
Unlimited PTO, company holidays, and quarterly mental health days

Comprehensive health benefits including medical, dental & vision, and parental leave
