title: Chief Technology Officer - US-Based
description:
About Toptal 

Toptal is a global network of top talent in business, design, and technology that enables companies to scale their teams, on-demand. With $200+ million in annual revenue and team members based around the globe , Toptal is the world’s largest fully remote workforce .

We take the best elements of virtual teams and combine them with a support structure that encourages innovation, social interaction, and fun. We see no borders, move at a fast pace, and are never afraid to break the mold.

Position Description:

As Chief Technology Officer, you will drive execution for the product and engineering teams and put AI at the core of everything the company builds. You will own Toptal’s full technical architecture and you will build it AI-first—utilizing best practices for agentic engineering. AI is not a workstream inside the engineer team—its core to it.

You will create and own the AI architecture and best practices the rest of the company utilizes. You will also own the initiatives that put agents into production. You should know how to build and fine-tune foundation models from the ground up, how to engineer best-in-class harnesses, and how to create best practices for agentic engineering that engineering teams adopt to 10x their productivity—without sacrificing quality. Your mindset will be that of a builder and an architect, someone who solves problems in the system itself. No problem will be too large or too small for you to solve yourself. You will set the technical direction and hold the cadenced meetings that turns technical strategy into working, production-ready outcomes. You will be in the design reviews and in the code, not adjacent to them. You will move fast, and you will ensure our engineering team is never the reason an initiative slows down.

You are the technical owner of all Toptal’s products. You will collaborate closely with Product to design infrastructure that exposes Toptal’s core business logic through modular interfaces the rest of the business can build on. Alongside a group of hands-on executives, your engineering discipline directly shapes Toptal’s growth, profitability, and operational excellence.

You will own resourcing and workforce planning as a doer: scoping the work, sizing the teams, planning headcount against it, defining the role and the bar for every seat. None of that is beneath the role, and we are not interested in someone who thinks these tasks can be done properly by handing it off to HR. Hiring is the highest-leverage work you do, and we want someone who is visibly excited about hiring A-players—with a sense of urgency.

Then, you lead the team. You will set the standards, develop people against those standards, and know exactly who is meeting those standards.

You will be one of Toptal’s foremost experts on AI, and you will stay ahead of a field that never stops moving. You will coach engineers on agentic best practices, show the executive team what is newly possible with the new AI tooling, and push AI into every function at Toptal.

This role runs on high-energy execution and attention to detail. You will bring urgency to every part of it and measure yourself on outcomes. We are not looking for someone to oversee this work. We are looking for someone to drive it and get into the details.

This is a remote position. Resumes and communication must be submitted in English.

Responsibilities:

The following information is intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed. It is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, or required skills. 

One precondition runs through all of it: you conceive the strategy. You will form your own view of where engineering and AI should go, build the case, and bring the CEO a strategy to react to, not a request for direction.

AI and agentic engineering 

- Own Toptal’s AI technology strategy and the architecture beneath it: model selection and fine-tuning, harness design, orchestration, retrieval, context engineering, tool and MCP integration, guardrails, evaluation, and cost control, exposed as primitives every team composes against.

- Deploy agentic engineering at scale against the work that runs this business: matching, vetting, onboarding, delivery, and internal operations. Own the outcomes those agents are accountable for.

- Make AI quality measurable. Own the evals, the regression suites, and the review loops, so quality here is proven rather than claimed.

- Rebuild how the platform gets built and operated, raising output per engineer through AI-assisted development, review, testing, and operations. Engineers have to want this, not comply with it, and creating that pull is on you.

Team, resourcing, and accountability 

- Decide what a team should look like now that the roles have blurred, where the product manager believes they can design and code, the engineer believes they can do product and design, and the designer believes they can code and do product.

- Own resourcing and workforce planning: scope the roadmap into buildable work, plan headcount and sequence, write the specs, and hit time-sensitive hiring commitments.

- Own the bar for the team: assess talent honestly, develop people against the bar, and hold it as the organization grows.

About Limbic 

Limbic’s vision is to ensure the highest quality therapy is accessible to everyone, everywhere.

Limbic has supported more than 820,000 patients across the UK and the US. We are used in over 50% of NHS Talking Therapies services, which makes us the largest-ever deployment of generative AI for direct patient care, and our AI now delivers end-to-end therapy to patients in the US under the supervision of licensed clinicians.

Safety and science come first. We are the only AI mental health chatbot with UKCA Class IIa medical device certification, and the first AI-led mental healthcare company selected for the FDA’s TEMPO pilot. Our results are published in leading scientific journals: in a randomized, double-blind trial published in Nature Medicine, our AI agents scored higher than licensed CBT therapists on a standard measure of therapy skill.

The Role 

As a Senior AI/ML Engineer, you will take ownership of the AI in our clinical assessment product for US healthcare organizations. A patient describes what they are struggling with in a conversation with our AI, which gathers their history, administers standard clinical questionnaires such as PHQ-9 and GAD-7, detects risk and recommends a treatment program for the organization’s clinicians to review. Every organization configures it for its own services, so the AI has to be safe and accurate across many clinical setups, not just one.

The approach is proven at scale in the NHS, where it increased referrals from minority groups by 29%, as published in Nature Medicine. - 
Productionize ML models that optimize product KPIs, including the accuracy of clinical predictions and how quickly patients reach the right care.

- 
Build and maintain evaluation harnesses, simulated patient conversations and labelled transcript review, so every configuration can be tested before a patient sees it.

-

- 
Help turn our clinical AI into composable services that healthcare partners can integrate into their own patient journeys.

-

A PhD in computational science or an AI-related field, plus 2 years of experience in an ML engineering role.

Expertise in productizing LLM features and a strong background in eval-driven development.

- 
Expert-level proficiency in Python and TypeScript/JavaScript.

- 
Proven experience building an LLM agent harness .

- 
Experience utilizing reinforcement learning.

- 
Strong architectural skills with experience designing scalable, production-grade systems for machine learning applications.

Hands-on experience with a major cloud platform and containerization technologies.

North American business hours (Eastern time preferred), with daily overlap with colleagues in Europe (UTC to UTC+3).

Based in Canada with the right to work there.

25 days PTO.

Support with purchasing work-related books and materials.

title: Critical Infrastructure Engineering Lead
description:
About Mistral 

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

Our mission 

Serve as Mistral AI’s senior technical authority for critical electrical, mechanical and life-safety infrastructure across assigned colocation sites. Protect the availability of high-density AI compute by identifying technical risks before they become incidents, challenging infrastructure operating practices and verifying that power and cooling systems perform within agreed requirements.

Operating context & accountability 

Working with Engineering Operations leadership, IT Operations, hardware partners and colocation providers, you will provide hands-on technical assurance across a site or cluster. You will assess provider performance, advise on critical decisions, support incident response and ensure operational learning drives durable improvements. The role focuses on technical oversight and influence rather than direct management of the colocation provider’s maintenance workforce.

Technical assurance and operational risk 

- Own and maintain the site technical risk register, including electrical and mechanical single points of failure, maintenance exposure, redundancy limitations, cooling capacity, liquid-cooling interfaces and common-mode failure scenarios.

- Assess the resilience of utility connections, MV/LV distribution, transformers, generators, UPS, switchgear, busways, protection systems, pumps, cooling plant, controls and monitoring against the contracted operating envelope.

- Review provider preventive maintenance strategies, schedules, critical asset condition and outstanding defects; identify maintenance deferrals and vulnerabilities that may affect AI compute availability.

- Critically review high-risk methods of procedure, electrical switching and isolation plans, planned impairments, work sequencing, contingency measures, rollback plans and restoration criteria.

- Validate the completeness and quality of technical documentation, including single-line diagrams, P&IDs, operating sequences, alarm matrices, capacity records, asset registers and operating procedures.

- Use BMS/EPMS trends, alarms, power-quality records and cooling telemetry to identify abnormal operating conditions, capacity constraints and deteriorating resilience before service is affected.

Incident response, investigations and reliability 

- Act as a senior engineering escalation point during major infrastructure incidents; rapidly assess failure domain, remaining redundancy, safety implications, likely IT impact and viable restoration options.

- Coordinate technical information across the colocation provider, Mistral IT Operations and OEM partners, ensuring accurate incident timelines, risk communication and controlled return to service.

- Review and challenge root-cause analyses, distinguishing immediate triggers from underlying design, maintenance, controls, process and organizational contributors.

- Define and follow up corrective and preventive actions, requesting evidence of implementation and verifying that recurring failure modes have been addressed.

- Identify systemic trends across sites and share lessons learned with engineering design, commissioning and regional operations teams.

- Support emergency response planning and tabletop exercises covering loss of utility, cooling failures, liquid leaks, fire/life-safety events and critical equipment failures.

Capacity delivery, commissioning and change control 

- Participate in design and constructability reviews for expansions, retrofits and new AI deployments; flag operational, maintainability and resilience concerns early.

- Review commissioning and integrated systems testing plans, including power transfers, redundancy scenarios, controls failure modes, cooling recovery and operational readiness criteria.

- Challenge test results and acceptance evidence against defined electrical, thermal and operational requirements; track unresolved technical issues through handover.

- Partner with IT Operations on rack power and thermal limits, direct-to-chip liquid cooling, coolant distribution unit boundaries, leak response and load-restoration dependencies.

- Assess proposed changes to critical infrastructure, including concurrent maintenance, controls updates and brownfield works; recommend safeguards and escalation where exposure is unacceptable.

- Provide technical coaching to internal stakeholders, contribute to engineering standards and support recruitment and knowledge sharing as the portfolio expands.

Success measures 

- Critical technical risks are identified early, prioritized and reduced through verified mitigation actions, supporting Mistral’s availability objectives.

- High-risk maintenance and infrastructure changes receive timely, evidence-based technical review with clear mitigations and escalation.

- Major incidents are diagnosed accurately, communicated effectively and followed by robust root-cause analysis and verified corrective actions.

- New and expanded capacity meets agreed redundancy, electrical, cooling and operational acceptance requirements.

- Repeat failures, unresolved high-severity defects and preventable technical deviations decrease over time.

Minimum qualifications 

- 5–7+ years in critical facilities engineering, commissioning, data center operations or technical assurance in high-availability environments.

- Strong practical knowledge of critical electrical infrastructure (UPS, generators, MV/LV distribution, switchgear and protection) and mechanical systems (cooling plant, pumps, controls and heat rejection).

- Ability to review single-line diagrams, operating sequences, technical procedures, maintenance plans, commissioning evidence and root-cause analyses.

- Demonstrated experience troubleshooting complex infrastructure incidents and influencing external technical teams without direct line authority.

- Clear written and verbal English communication, sound judgment under pressure and willingness to travel and participate in incident escalation as needed.

Preferred experience 

- Full technical governance, multi-site operations or mission-critical facilities serving high-density AI/HPC workloads.

- Experience with direct-to-chip liquid cooling, CDUs, facility/technology cooling interfaces, water quality, leak detection and rack-level thermal management.

- Integrated systems testing, EPMS/BMS trend analysis, protection coordination, failure-mode reviews and cross-site engineering standardization.

- Experience partnering with hardware OEMs, design engineers, commissioning teams and infrastructure providers during live-site expansion.

What We Offer 

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page .

Privacy Policy 

Your privacy matters to us. You can learn more about how we handle your personal data in our Applicant Privacy Policy .

title: Senior Data Scientist, Trust & Safety
description:
Brief info about Vinted 

Our mission is to make second-hand the first choice, and we're looking for people who want to help us get there. Every day, we work together to help our members buy and sell pre-loved clothing and lifestyle items, giving each piece a second life – or even a third. 
The Vinted Group is made up of three business units that support this mission:

Vinted Marketplace is Europe’s leading platform for second-hand fashion and a go-to destination for all kinds of pre-loved items, with a growing range of categories. Our platform connects millions of members across 20+ markets, helping great items find a new life.

Vinted Go enhances the shipping experience with a vast network of over 500,000 pick-up and drop-off points, partnering with more than 60 carriers across Europe, with added services like item verification for peace of mind on high-value pieces.

Vinted Pay is the newest part of the Vinted Group, dedicated to bringing secure, reliable payments to buyers and sellers across Europe. Seamlessly integrated into the Vinted app, it helps keep every transaction safe, efficient, and easy for our members.

Founded in 2008 in Lithuania, Vinted began as a way for friends to find new homes for clothes they no longer needed. In 2019, we became Lithuania's first unicorn! Today, our headquarters remain in Vilnius, and we've grown with offices across Europe, supported by a team of over 2,000 people. 

Information about the position 

You’ll join Trust & Safety’s Actioning team, whose mission is to protect the Vinted community from harmful activities and content. The team owns critical mechanisms, including user reporting, moderation workflows, policy enforcement, and interventions against malicious users.

You will leverage your expertise in machine learning to research, design and implement new models for report and appeals prioritization, advanced sanctioning based on users' suspicions, and automation of moderation decisions. This involves working closely with our engineering teams to develop robust pipelines for data handling, feature engineering, model training, deployment, and continuous improvement. 

As a Senior Data Scientist, you will utilize advanced machine learning techniques to analyze text, images, and other data formats, tackling complex challenges to identify and address content that poses potential risks. You will champion best practices and methodologies, significantly enhancing the team's effectiveness and safeguarding Vinted. You will mentor others, influence the strategic direction for model development, and facilitate cross-functional collaborations to drive impactful results.

In this position, you’ll 

- Lead the research, development, and end-to-end lifecycle of production machine learning models that prioritize and automate actions on harmful marketplace entities at scale.

- Play a crucial role in establishing and refining essential machine learning processes, such as data versioning, creating labeling pipelines, and ensuring high-quality data availability for effective model training.

- Actively collaborate across teams, particularly with Data Infrastructure and backend engineers, to develop and maintain scalable data pipelines and infrastructure, ensuring optimal performance and scalability of deployed models.

- Influence and contribute to the strategic roadmap for the Actioning team, collaborating with Decision Scientists to test, assess, and continuously improve new models.

About you 

- Proven track record in data science (4+ years of experience), with a strong foundation in machine learning, statistics, or computational mathematics.

- Proficiency in both classical and deep learning techniques, and an adeptness in leveraging the latest tools and methodologies to solve complex problems.

- Hands-on experience building and deploying agentic AI applications or LLM-powered workflows that handle large traffic, balancing quality, latency, and cost efficiency.

- Deep understanding of the challenges involved in deploying, maintaining, and scaling real-time ML models in production, with a proven ability to address these challenges effectively.

- Proven capability to work with engineering teams, designing and implementing efficient data ingestion, feature engineering, and model training pipelines that support robust and reliable model deployment.

- Excellent problem-solving abilities, with a commitment to staying at the forefront of developments in machine learning and data science, driving innovation and thought leadership within the team.

- Ability to clearly communicate complex ideas and technical concepts to both technical and non-technical stakeholders, ensuring that technical elements are properly understood and integrated to deliver business value.

- Past experience with fraud detection, harmful content detection or any other adversarial domain would be considered an advantage. 

Work perks 

- The opportunity to benefit from our share options programme

- 25 days of paid annual leave

- Newest MacBook models

- Confidential Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for you and your family

- Frequent team-building events

- Home office support: we provide IT workstation equipment and a personal budget of up to €540 for home workplace furniture

- Lunch benefit per working day

- A personal monthly budget for shopping on Vinted

- Collective Defined Contribution Pension plan

- NS Business Card for your commute to the office by public transport

- Company bike leasing scheme

Better balance holidays with workdays by working remotely! Up to 90 days per year in the EU, of these, 21 days can be spent globally. For non-EU citizens, it's 21 days worldwide. This can be combined with time off for vacation or personal time.

Individual learning budget 

Each year, you’ll be given a learning budget (starting at €3,000), and a total of up to 10 working days over a 2-year period to support your personal and professional development.

Hybrid work 

Our hybrid model, with 2 recommended office days a week, gives you and your team the flexibility to decide if and when you want to work from home, and when to catch up in person.

Equal opportunity

Nice-to-have skills

About Canonical 

Canonical is a pioneering tech firm at the forefront of the global move to open source. As the company that publishes Ubuntu, one of the most important open source projects and the platform for AI, IoT and the cloud, we are changing the world of software. We recruit on a global basis and set a very high standard for people joining the company. We expect excellence - in order to succeed, we need to be the best at what we do. title: Cardog | Toronto, Canada or REMOTE | Full-time
description:
Cardog | Toronto, Canada or REMOTE | Full-time
https://cardog.app/careers We're the system of record for the Canadian vehicle: raw automotive data turned into facts that can be checked. Our open-source VIN decoder sits underneath a government vehicle registry. Some of what's interesting: - A government registry, a manufacturer's own filing, a listing site and an insurance record will describe the same truck four different ways, and nothing in any of those files says they're the same truck. Reconciling that, for every vehicle in the country, in a way that holds up when a regulator asks how you know, is most of the data work. - Seventeen characters on a door frame encode manufacturer, plant, model year and build attributes — badly, inconsistently, and differently per manufacturer. Public reference data covers some of it. The rest gets worked out from filings, recall documents, and patterns inferred across millions of vehicles. - We read vehicles directly over OBD-II now. Forty modules answered on a recent Hyundai, each reporting its own part number and installed software version. Nothing downstream of the VIN moves when a module is reflashed, so no registration, history report or dealer system knows what software is actually in a car. Hiring: VIN Decode Engineer, Data Platform Engineer, Infrastructure Engineer, Founding Engineer (dealer platform). TypeScript, Postgres, Cloudflare Workers. Full descriptions and apply: https://cardog.app/careers

title: Abuse Research Engineer
description:
Headquarters: Remote from the US

Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career. 

About the team

Abuse Research Group (ARG) handles proactive threat hunting and adversary behavior analysis across Stripe products. Rather than reacting to alerts, the team maps end-to-end fraud and abuse paths, validates novel attack vectors, and identifies product conditions that enable fraud. Using agentic automated testing and simulation tools, ARG translates research into actionable threat advisories, strategic control recommendations, and regression scenarios to systematically eliminate vulnerabilities.

What you’ll do

As an Abuse Research Engineer in the Abuse Research Group, you will play a critical role in safeguarding Stripe’s financial ecosystem by proactively hunting for advanced threats, dissecting complex fraud vectors, and extracting actionable adversary intelligence. Rather than relying solely on reactive alerts, you will develop and execute hypothesis-driven threat hunting operations across internal telemetry and external sources to uncover fraudulent tools, tactics, and techniques (TTPs) before they impact Stripe’s platform. Central to this work is FT3 (Fraud Taxonomy 3.0), Stripe’s multi-layered taxonomy that decomposes monolithic fraud into structured kill chains. Collaborating cross-functionally with Fraud Ops, Strategy, Risk, Onboarding, and Security, you will integrate threat intelligence, build agentic simulation workflows, and systematically eliminate product vulnerabilities.

Responsibilities

- Proactive Threat Hunting & Kill Chain Analysis: Formulate hypotheses and conduct iterative threat hunting operations across Stripe systems and external data.

- FT3 Taxonomy: Apply and enrich the FT3 framework across empirical datasets and incidents, standardizing threat intelligence across kill chain phases and targeted API endpoints. 

- Threat Intelligence & Signal Expansion: Partner with teams like Fraud Intelligence to integrate, curate, and automate threat feeds into engineering workflows. 

- Cross-Functional Advisories & Strategic Controls: Translate raw research and retrospective findings into actionable threat advisories and control recommendations (policy, technical systems, support workflows, and detection mechanisms) for stakeholders across Fraud, Risk, Onboarding, and Security. 

- Agentic Testing & Adversary Simulation: Utilize agentic automated testing frameworks to simulate adversary TTPs, validate whether deployed controls interrupt empirical kill chains, and generate regression scenarios to exercise controls. 

Who you are 

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement. 

Minimum requirements

- 5+ years of experience conducting threat intelligence, threat hunting, or technical incident response within cyber security, product abuse, or trust domains. 

- 5+ years of experience analyzing large, complex datasets using data analytics tools to identify anomalies, map behavioral trends, and solve complex fraud problems. 

- B.S. or M.S. in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience. 

- Expert proficiency in Python and SQL, with demonstrated experience using code and scripting to automate workflows, build investigative tools, or query big data pipelines. 

- Hands-on experience in log analysis (e.g., application logs, API route telemetry, network security events), digital forensics, and cyber investigation methodologies. 

- Strong communication skills with a proven ability to translate complex technical research into clear, actionable recommendations and advisories for cross-functional partners.

Preferred qualifications 

- Deep technical understanding of threat actor motivations, infrastructure, and TTPs specific to financial fraud (e.g., ATO, Card Testing, Credential Stuffing). 

- Familiarity with standardized taxonomies such as FT3 or MITRE ATT&CK. 

- Proficiency with engineering, data processing, and analysis platforms such as Databricks, Trino, PySpark, Pandas, or Scikit-Learn. 

- Proven background utilizing Threat Intelligence Platforms (TIPs), tactical threat feeds, OSINT, and breach intelligence. 

- Demonstrated capability building or leveraging agentic LLM tools, automated testing systems, or control validation frameworks to model adversary behavior at scale. 

- Participation in industry conferences, webinars, or threat-sharing groups, alongside relevant professional certifications (e.g., GCTI, GCFA, OSCP).

To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/stripe-abuse-research-engineer

What will give you an edge?

Cybersecurity experience

Running services on Kubernetes, ideally on GCP

Building complex applications or systems from the ground up with a cross-functional team

What's in it for you? 

We're fully remote, and we'd rather spend on things people actually use than on perks that look good in a job ad.

title: Experimentation & Tracking engineer
description:
🧡 About Alma

At Alma, we believe sustainable commerce depends on fair, well-balanced trade. Because finance plays a pivotal role in business, our mission is to put it back in its rightful place: serving merchants and consumers.

Our installment and deferred payment solutions help merchants boost sales by 20% or more, increase customer loyalty, and deliver a seamless shopping experience, without encouraging bad debt.

As the buy now pay later leader in France and active in 10 European countries, we've empowered over 25,000 merchants and 10 million consumers.

With 380+ Almakers and €100M+ ARR, Alma is scaling rapidly across Europe as a member of the Next40, and we're just getting started!

👐 About the team

You will join the Growth team and work closely with Revenue Operations, Account Managers, Business Analysts, Marketing, Data, and merchant technical teams. You will help Alma apply to its own website the experimentation and measurement expertise we bring to merchants.

This is a permanent, full-time position based in Paris, with a hybrid working model. Professional French and English are required.

💼 About the job

As an Experimentation & Tracking Engineer, you will own web experimentation at Alma: the A/B tests we run on merchant websites, the measurement of what happens on our own website, and its continued development following our recent redesign.

Your responsibilities will include:

Lead merchant experimentation from opportunity to readout 

- Qualify testing opportunities against technical and volume eligibility criteria, then design each test with the merchant: scenario, traffic split, pages, events, KPIs, duration, and stopping rule.

- Implement variations and event tracking in Kameleoon, run the live phase, check data quality, and present the first results to the merchant alongside the Account Manager and Business Analysts.

Own web tracking and measurement quality 

- Define and maintain the tracking plan for Alma's website across 8 markets, implementing it through GTM, GA4, or equivalent tools.

- Ensure reliable data flows into Salesforce, BigQuery, and Looker, while owning consent and GDPR compliance, deduplication, attribution, and reconciliation across sources.

Build and optimize almapay.com 

- Build and evolve landing pages, product pages, market pages, and local content following the website redesign.

- Run a CRO programme on Alma's own funnels, starting with the demo request, while maintaining performance, Core Web Vitals, technical SEO, and hreflang across markets.

Scale the experimentation practice 

- Turn the existing framework, documentation, and tooling into a repeatable practice, with a target of 8 merchant tests going live over the year.

- Share standards, learnings, and results with Growth, Revenue Operations, Data, Marketing, Sales, and Product stakeholders.

🧰 You will work with

Kameleoon, Google Tag Manager, Google Analytics 4, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, Salesforce, BigQuery, Looker, Looker Studio, Metabase, n8n, Make, Notion, Slack, GitHub.

🧩 About you

To succeed in this job

- You have 3 to 5 years of experience in experimentation, web analytics, CRO, or measurement-oriented web development.

- You have hands-on experience with GTM and GA4, or equivalent tools, including consent mode, data quality, and debugging issues that can fail silently.

- You are self-sufficient in JavaScript and HTML/CSS, including DOM manipulation, variation building, and debugging on websites you did not build and cannot fully control.

- You understand the fundamentals of test validity, including sample size, stopping rules, and what makes an experiment result trustworthy. You are also comfortable working with clients and technical stakeholders in French and English.

And it will be nice if you also

- Have an e-commerce or payments background, with familiarity with checkout journeys.

- Can use SQL to pull and investigate your own data.

- Have worked with Kameleoon, Optimizely, AB Tasty, VWO, or a similar experimentation platform.

- Speak Spanish, Italian, or German.

Don't meet every single requirement? At Alma, we believe great hires come from diverse paths. If this role excites you, we encourage you to apply. We value potential, curiosity, and the ability to grow as much as experience.

🧘 What's in it for you

If you join, you will be able to grow and impact on:

- Owning a broad, high-impact scope as Alma's internal reference for experimentation and tracking, with the autonomy to shape the practice.

- Seeing the direct business outcomes of your work: your tests inform how Alma wins and retains merchants, and your findings are presented to real customers.

- Working across dozens of merchant websites, 8 markets, and several CMS platforms, while being supported by a central Data team and Business Analysts for deeper analysis.

🤑 Compensation & Benefits

- Competitive salary based on 12 months

- Profit-sharing and employee savings plan

- Health insurance: 100% covered by Alma, including family package

- Disability insurance: 100% covered by Alma

- Sport: partnerships with Gymlib and ClassPass, or €30/month reimbursement for your sports activities

- Maternity/paternity leave: salary maintained at 100% during leave with no seniority requirement. Return to work at a 4/5 schedule paid at 100% for 8 weeks.

- Sustainable Mobility Package (FMD): €544.80/year, excluding full-remote contracts

- Meal vouchers: €10/day, 50% covered by Alma

- Mental health: free access to the MindDay platform

- Paid time off: 25 days/year, plus additional paid leave for employees on executive contracts

- Access to our Learning & Development Platform

- 2 weeks of full remote possible per year in summer

🎯 Interview Process

- Video call with a Talent Acquisition team member to understand your background and motivation, and present the role.

- Video call with the hiring manager from Revenue Operations & Growth to discuss the role, the team, your experience, and your questions.

- Practical case: scope an A/B test from a real merchant scenario and present your approach, including project management.

- Cross-interviews with a Sales or Account Management stakeholder and a Business Analyst you will work with.

- Final conversation with leadership.

🌍 Diversity & Inclusion

At Alma, we believe that diversity fuels innovation and makes our community stronger. We are committed to building a workplace where every person feels seen, respected, and empowered to do their best work whatever their gender, background, ethnicity, age, sexual orientation, religion, disability, or lived experience. As an equal opportunity employer, we welcome applicants from all walks of life, and all employment decisions are made based on qualifications, merit, and business needs.

title: Engineering - Internal AI Transformation
description:
About ElevenLabs

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

- ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

- ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

- ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.

How we work

- High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

- Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

- AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

- Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

- Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.

What we offer

- Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

- Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

- Learning & development : ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

- Social travel : We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

- Annual company offsite: Each year, we bring the entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia and Italy.

- Co-working : If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

The role / impact 
As an Internal AI Engineer at ElevenLabs, you'll be embedded at the frontier of how we scale - acting as a forward-deployed engineer across our GTM, Operations, and Finance teams. You won't just build tools; you'll co-design and ship agentic AI workflows that eliminate manual toil and fundamentally reshape how our people operate.

Your impact goes beyond the code. You'll own high-stakes automations from discovery to production, acting as a technical partner to internal teams. The patterns, guardrails, and tooling you define will become the blueprint other teams reach for - the standard for how ElevenLabs harnesses AI safely and at speed.

The team / how we work 
You'll join a lean, high-velocity team with a shared obsession: turning broken, manual processes into elegant automated systems. We move fast through rapid experimentation, work closely with operators and business owners to uncover the real problem, and ship pragmatic solutions without waiting for perfect specs.

What you'll actually be working on 

- Designing and iterating on AI agents and workflow orchestrations using tools like ElevenAgents, Claude, and n8n.

- Integrating AI systems with our core business stack - Salesforce, Slack, Ashby, and more

- Building reusable automation services, patterns and shared templates that multiply the output of every team you touch

- Owning experiments end-to-end: spotting the opportunity, building the solution, and measuring the impact

- Developing evaluation and monitoring frameworks so our AI-native workflows are reliable, auditable, and safe

What we're looking for 

- Proven experience building and shipping automations or applications in production - you know what it takes to go from fuzzy business pain to something real teams depend on

- AI-First Instincts: Strong familiarity with LLM capabilities, prompting strategies, RAG patterns, and a genuine passion for building agentic workflows.

- Deep Backend Expertise : Strong Python and SQL and system design patterns (APIs, webhooks, orchestration layers)

- A systems-thinking mindset : you design with security, auditability, and blast radius in mind from the start

- Builder and AI-First instincts: you don't wait to be told what to build - you spot the pattern, propose the fix, and ship it.

- Infra & DevOps Instincts: Hands-on experience operating cloud infrastructure (GCP preferred), Kubernetes, Docker, and enterprise authentication flows

Location

This role is remote and can be executed globally. If you prefer, you can work from our offices in London, New York, San Francisco, and Warsaw. Specific teams may have specific location preferences.

We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability or other legally protected statuses.

title: Data Engineer
description:
Een pipeline die 's nachts breekt? Jij levert de structurele fix, niet de workaround. Een query die te veel kost? Jij ziet meteen waar het misgaat. Bij Follo leunt performance marketing volledig op data die klopt: elke bieding, elk klantrapport en elk AI-model dat we inzetten hangt af van de pipelines die data uit allerlei bronnen naar ons datawarehouse brengen. 

Wij geloven dat daar de toekomst ligt, dus we blijven doorbouwen en investeren de komende jaren flink in onze data-infrastructuur. Daarvoor zoeken we iemand die weet hoe je datastructuren neerzet, monitort en zo kostenefficiënt mogelijk laat draaien. Je bouwt zowel de warehouses als de pipelines en zorgt dat alles feilloos functioneert. Je denkt vanuit architectuur en kiest oplossingen die er over twee jaar nog staan, ook als de tooling eromheen verandert. Tegelijk snap je dat een agency snel moet kunnen schakelen. Dat evenwicht is waar deze rol om draait. 

Wat je gaat doen 

- Je ontwerpt, bouwt en beheert ETL- en ELT-workflows die meegroeien met het aantal klanten. 

- Je orkestreert datastromen via DAG-platforms. We werken nu met Windmill en onderzoeken een migratie naar een platform dat beter past bij onze stabiliteitseisen. Jij hebt daar een zwaarwegende stem in. 

- Je schrijft onderhoudbare Python en TypeScript voor koppelingen en transformaties. 

- Je bewaakt kwaliteit, uptime en betrouwbaarheid. Breekt er een pipeline, dan lever jij de structurele fix en niet de tijdelijke workaround. 

- Je zet LLM's in als vaste transformatiestap in pipelines, bijvoorbeeld voor het opschonen, categoriseren of verrijken van bulkdata. 

- Je houdt de kosten scherp: je optimaliseert zware BigQuery-queries, voorkomt overbodige API-calls en gaat bewust om met tokenverbruik. 

Onze stack 

BigQuery, Google Cloud Platform, Windmill, Python, TypeScript en PHP/Laravel voor onze main app, GitHub met CI/CD, en de API's van OpenAI, Anthropic en Google Gemini. Voor infrabeheer werken we met Terraform en Ansible, voor monitoring en telemetrie met Sentry, Slack Applications, Grafana, Loki en InfluxDB. Zie je een beter alternatief? Dan horen we dat graag. 

Het team 

Je komt in een klein engineeringteam van twee engineers dat de komende jaren verder groeit. Je rapporteert rechtstreeks aan de coördinator / team lead, dus de lijn naar besluitvorming is kort en je hoeft niet te wachten tot iemand jouw idee doorgeeft. 

Wat je van ons mag verwachten 

- Een salaris passend bij je ervaring en expertise. 

- 26 vakantiedagen per jaar, met de mogelijkheid om er 5 bij te kopen. 

- Een eenmalig thuiswerkbudget tot €1.000 om je thuiswerkplek goed in te richten. 

- Een goed geregeld pensioen, zonder eigen bijdrage. 

- De vrijheid om hybride te werken, en maximaal 3 maanden per jaar remote vanuit het buitenland. 

- Toegang tot BigQuery, GCP, DAG-platforms en de betaalde API's van de grote LLM-aanbieders. 

- Interne kennissessies en deep-dives over data-engineering en AI. 

Dit ben jij 

Je hebt minimaal 2 tot 3 jaar ervaring met data-engineering in productie en je denkt vanuit architectuur, niet vanuit losse taken. Verder: 

Wat we echt nodig hebben 

- Je schrijft robuuste, productieklare code in Python en TypeScript. 

- Je hebt aantoonbaar ETL- of ELT-workflows gebouwd en onderhouden waar anderen op vertrouwden. 

- Je bent sterk in SQL en BigQuery: complexe queries, window functions en datamodellering. 

- Je hebt met minstens één DAG-platform gewerkt, bijvoorbeeld Windmill, Airflow, Dagster, Prefect, Inngest of Temporal. 

- Je past versiebeheer en CI/CD toe op data-infrastructuur. 

- Je hebt 2 tot 3 jaar ervaring met Google Cloud Platform en kunt een bestaande omgeving doorgronden, beoordelen en opnieuw opzetten waar dat nodig is. 

Mooi als je dit meebrengt 

- Een Google Cloud certificering: minimaal Professional Data Engineer en bij voorkeur ook Professional Cloud Architect . Voor ons is dat geen vinkje: het laat zien dat je het platform echt beheerst en het is essentieel voor onze Google Cloud Partnership-status. 

- Ervaring met LLM's in geautomatiseerde dataprocessen. 

- Ervaring met PHP of Laravel, voor de integratie met onze main app. 

- Ervaring met het migreren tussen orchestratieplatformen. 

- Oog voor FinOps en cloudkosten. 

Herken je jezelf in het grootste deel hiervan, maar niet in alles? Solliciteer alsnog. 

Waarom Follo? 

Bij Follo lopen we voorop in een landschap dat razendsnel verandert, en we bouwen daar actief aan mee. AI is bij ons geen buzzword, maar onderdeel van hoe we dagelijks werken. Denk aan MCP-koppelingen, geautomatiseerde workflows en LLM's als vaste stap in onze dataverwerking. 

- Je bouwt aan de infrastructuur waar het hele bureau dagelijks op draait: elke bieding en elk rapport begint bij jouw pipelines. 

- Echte invloed op architectuur en toolkeuze, inclusief de migratie van ons orchestratieplatform. 

- AI zit in ons DNA: van FolloEngine tot LLM's als vaste stap in productie-pipelines. 

- Sterke merken en echte uitdagingen, in een bureau met Europese ambities. 

Zin om bij Follo te werken? 

Meld je dan direct aan. Heb je nog vragen? Stuur onze recruiter een mail via . Tot snel!

title: GTM Engineer - Growth
description:
We believe conversations will become the #1 way to shop. 

At Gorgias, we’re building the platform that makes this real: a unified AI agent that sells, supports, and re-engages customers across the entire journey. Conversational Commerce is the future of ecommerce, and we’re leading that shift.

Our mission is to turn every interaction between a brand and its customers into a relationship: personal, seamless, and intelligent. By combining deep product expertise with the latest in AI, we’re making shopping feel more natural, human, and connected than ever before.

To win, we focus relentlessly on:

- Quality: conversations that feel authentic and on-brand.

- Experience: effortless shopping from chat to checkout.

- Re-engagement: personal, 1-1 dialogue instead of noisy marketing.

The opportunity is massive. As AI reshapes how people buy, Gorgias is building the foundation for the next decade of ecommerce, where every brand has its own intelligent agent and every customer feels understood.

Join us to make Conversational Commerce real.

About the Team

GTM Engineers builds the AI product layer for Gorgias's go-to-market teams: AI agents, internal cockpits, and the automations underneath them, all running on one shared context layer (Cortex). We work across Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, and Partnerships. We build and maintain the agents, the business teams own the outputs, and humans review exceptions.

About the Role

You'll own the AI agents that run Gorgias's GTM workflows, taking them from manual process to reviewed agent. The goal is to optimize as much GTM work as possible without losing quality. A strong fit ships working agents quickly, debugs a broken workflow in Cargo, HubSpot, or another GTM tool without waiting for help, and cares whether the business actually uses what gets built.

What You'll Do

- Navigate between our context layer, our app and service repositories, MCPs, and our automation tools to build and improve end-to-end GTM workflows.

- Build custom agents and reusable agent skills on our agent stack (Cortex) , and on custom builds when the stack can't do the job.

- Build and maintain agents for lead and account work: outbound reply handling, audience and call-list building, enrichment, event follow-up, and referral routing.

- Map the Sales and Marketing workflow backlog, decide Agent vs. Automation vs. Manual for each workflow, and deliver the chosen option with a reviewable output for the business owner.

- Improve live agents: tune prompts and skills, read conversation and performance data, fix regressions, and document edge cases.

- Debug broken workflows fast across Cargo, HubSpot, Customer.io , and other GTM tools, and fix the root cause.

- Connect agents to our systems through APIs and workflows (n8n, Clay, custom code), with credentials managed centrally rather than on personal accounts.

- Help Sales (BDRs and AEs) and CS adopt agents: learn their daily work, design flows with them, and train them to supervise outputs.

- Work with the other GTM Engineers (cockpit, data, systems) so agents run on clean CRM data.

Who You Are

- You need to be passionate about AI. Claude Code, Conductor, or another AI coding harness is where you spend most of your time building—not something you only experiment with occasionally.

- 3+ years in a technical GTM, RevOps, or growth engineering role, with production automations you can point to.

- Hands-on with LLM applications: prompt design, tool or function calling, and reviewing output quality. Experience building custom agents is a plus.

- Familiarity with a modern data stack (BigQuery, dbt, Segment, Airbyte, Hightouch) is a plus.

- Solid SQL and Python or JavaScript, and comfortable working with REST APIs.

- Working knowledge on outbound or engagement tool (Cargo, Dust, Apollo, Lemlist, Instantly, Customer.io , or similar).

- Experience with n8n, Clay, or a similar automation tool is a plus.

- Good business judgment: you know when an agent should draft and when it should act.

- Ownership: you take a workflow from idea to live agent and flag breakages early.

- Fluent English. French is a plus for the Paris team.

Perks & Benefits 

- 🏖️ 5-week vacation plus 2 weeks RTT (We follow each country's appropriate PTO Laws)

- 🤕 Paid sick leave

- 🧸 Paid parental leave (16 weeks)

title: AI Engineer (Agentic AI)
description:
Legal AI is only as good as the knowledge behind it. At Lefebvre Sdu, we’ve been building that knowledge for 200 years. Day in, day out. Law by law. Word by word. Other legal AI tools run on our data and software. As the Dutch heart of Lefebvre Group, the European leader in legal and tax knowledge, we’re also developing our own platform: GenIA-L, where lawyers and tax professionals don’t just get an answer, but an answer they’re willing to put their name to. More than 75,000 professionals use it every day, accounting for over €100 million ARR across Europe. We’re looking for a Medior AI Engineer to help shape how the intelligent core of that platform evolves.

HOW YOU'LL MOVE US FORWARD 

GenIA-L is a research platform for legal professionals. A user asks a question. The platform searches our trusted sources and turns them into a useful answer. It does this with agents: specialised AI components that each handle part of the question and work together. In the legal domain, an answer can't just sound fluent. It has to be correct, and you must be able to see which source it comes from. This is not a pilot project: the platform runs in production and is used heavily every day.

As a medior, your focus is on building. You work independently, on challenges that come from customers and on challenges we spot ourselves. You break down a legal process, translate it into a technical process and work out how to best connect the pieces. Stuck on something? You say so, and your colleagues think along with you.

You build and improve the agents of GenIA-L and the way they work together.

You build and maintain our knowledge packages: for each legal article, an expert-validated set of commentary, case law, parliamentary history and practical interpretation. You also work on the pipelines that create these packages and keep them up to date.

You make quality measurable. With evaluation sets, observability and metrics, you show that answers, source attribution and reliability really improve. Not by gut feeling, but with evidence.

You build features for customers, such as analysing their own documents and new ways to search case law.

You work directly with editors and subject-matter experts, and check with them which parts of a legal question really matter.

You come up with and test ideas to make the product sharper or faster, and alternate AI experiments with back-end development.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR 

You have a realistic view of LLMs. You see what they can do, but you also know their weak spots. You enjoy following new AI developments, but you don't just follow the herd: you stay critical. You think in a structured way and can break a complex problem into smaller pieces. You work independently, take initiative when things are unclear and are eager to learn fast. And you enjoy working with lawyers and editors, because they know what a good answer looks like.

- You have several years of experience in software or ML engineering. Depth in recent projects counts for more than years.

- Strong experience in agentic AI. 

- You have good knowledge of Python and experience with relevant machine learning libraries.

- You have helped build an LLM application that runs in production. Not just prototypes, notebooks or courses.

- You have hands-on experience with agent frameworks such as LangGraph and LangChain, tool calling, MCP or comparable orchestration. Our entire product is built around this. Experience with only a simple search-and-answer (RAG) setup is not enough.

- You have measured the quality of an LLM system with evaluation sets or observability, and can give a concrete example. Experience with tools like MLflow and LiteLLM is a plus.

- You have back-end experience, including building REST APIs.

- You have experience in Kubernetes. Experience with Postgres is useful.

- Experience in a legal, tax or other knowledge-intensive domain is a plus.

WHAT YOU'RE SIGNING UP FOR 

On Tuesdays and Thursdays, the team works together at the office. What colleagues value most here: mutual trust, room to experiment, and a team that helps each other out when someone gets stuck.

- A place where you have influence from day one: on the approach, the processes, and the direction.

- Colleagues who deliberately chose Lefebvre Sdu over big tech jobs because here, they're building something that doesn't exist yet.

- Base salary between €4,477 and €5,793 per month, based on a 36-hour week, since that's full-time for us. Plus a lot of extra allowances (see below).

- A bonus tied to company performance: a fixed year-end bonus of 4% and profit sharing of up to 6%.

- 23 vacation days and a personal choice budget of 12%, of which 8% is holiday pay and 4% is freely allocable. Want more vacation? Just buy it.

- A bonus of up to 10% of your salary, based on company performance and individual performance.

- A solid pension plan through PGB, including supplementary partner insurance.

- Collective insurance plans.

- A travel allowance of €0.25 per kilometer or a public transport reimbursement, plus an attractive bike plan. For employees with a commute of less than 10 km or more than 60 km, we have an adjusted arrangement.

- Two days a week in the office in The Hague, within walking distance of Voorburg station. The rest of the week, wherever you work best.

- Room to grow: in your craft, in your role, in the organization.

WANT TO KNOW MORE? 

We'd love to tell you everything about the team and the role. Send us your CV and you'll hear from us within 2 working days. Any questions first? Text or call Nadine at 0628556265.

A reference check and a VOG (certificate of good behaviour) are part of the selection process.

title: Data Center Hardware Engineer
description:
About Mistral 

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

The mission 

You will work every day on the racks that power one of France's largest AI clusters.

Mistral's compute footprint is our single largest investment and the foundation of our AI research and engineering. We're hiring Data Center Hardware Engineers to keep our GPU/CPU clusters healthy, safe and growing — hands-on, in the data center, at the intersection of high-performance computing and physical infrastructure.

You'll join a small, senior team working at a scale few engineers get to experience: GPU-dense racks (H100/H200-class and next-generation platforms), high-speed interconnects, liquid-cooled systems — with new sites under development in France and beyond.

Hardware here is not someone else's problem. As part of a small on-site team, you carry responsibility for it end to end.

Location: On-site at one of our data center in Bessé-sur-Braye, Pays de la Loire.

What you'll do 

- Diagnose & repair server and cluster hardware: CPUs, memory, drives, NICs, GPUs, PSUs, and interconnect problems (switches, cables, transceivers; Ethernet/InfiniBand).

- Intervene safely — power-off/lockout, ESD discipline, pre/post-work checklists, tidy and safe work areas.

- Capture everything — photos, serials, test results; open, update and close tickets with notes the next engineer can act on.

- Manage parts — receive, label and track inventory; run RMAs and coordinate with vendors.

- Help us get better — feed recurring anomalies into monitoring, alerts and SOPs; contribute small scripts (Python/Bash) if you have those skills.

- Be a good teammate — clear status updates, honest handovers, and respect for the people depending on the cluster.

About you 

- Hands-on comfort in data centers or server hardware — you can (or will quickly learn to) work cleanly in racks: rails, cabling, labeling, mounting.

- Disciplined and meticulous: checklists aren't bureaucracy to you, they're craftsmanship.

- Practical electrical basics: power-off procedures, PPE, short-circuit risk awareness.

- Basic Linux (boot checks, logs) — scripting is a plus, not a requirement.

- Physically able to work in racks (lift, mount, maneuver) in a data center environment.

- Comfortable in a 24/7 operation, including a rotating on-call with emergency response expectations.

- Driver's licence (B) for travel between our sites.

Even if you don't match every criterion 

Many of our best hardware engineers came from research labs, telecoms, IT services or the military. If you are rigorous, curious and genuinely motivated by hardware at scale, we would be glad to hear from you — we assess demonstrated scope rather than keyword matching.

Nice to have 

- HPC/AI/cloud production experience at scale; large-fleet server install and maintenance.

- Networking fundamentals (Ethernet/InfiniBand) beyond basics.

- Vendor/RMA tooling, ticketing (Jira/ServiceNow), inventory systems.

- Python/Bash automation for checks, capture, inventory or reporting.

What We Offer 

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page .

Privacy Policy 

Your privacy matters to us. You can learn more about how we handle your personal data in our Applicant Privacy Policy .

title: Staff Software Security Engineer
description:
About Anthropic 

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role 

The Security Engineering team's mission is to safeguard our AI systems and maintain the trust of our users and society at large. Whether we're developing critical security infrastructure, building secure development practices, or partnering with our research and product teams, we are committed to operating as a world-class security organization and keeping the safety and trust of our users at the forefront of everything we do.

Responsibilities: 

- Build security for large-scale AI clusters across multiple clouds and bare-metal data centers, including IAM, network segmentation and encryption controls

- Design and implement network security controls: default-deny ingress and egress, segmentation between research, training and production environments, private connectivity across clouds and data centers, cloud firewall policy and mTLS with service identity

- Ship these controls as secure defaults using infrastructure as code and GitOps workflows, so new clusters, VPCs and data center links inherit the right boundaries

- Build visibility into network traffic and boundary drift, with detection for exfiltration paths and automated remediation where it is safe to do so

- Design secure-by-design development workflows and CI/CD pipelines across our services, with expertise in Kubernetes security, container orchestration and identity management

- Threat model and assess risk for complex multi cloud and networked environments, and join infrastructure networking, cluster and data center teams at design time so topology, routing and firewall decisions carry our security requirements from day one

- Mentor engineers and contribute to hiring and growth of the Security team

You may be a good fit if you:

- Have 8-15+ years of software engineering experience implementing and maintaining critical systems at scale

- Strong software engineering skills in Python or at least one systems language (Go, Rust, C/C++)

- Experience implementing and operating critical systems at scale using DevOps and cloud automation practices such as infrastructure as code

- Hands-on network security engineering in cloud or on-prem environments, for example VPC design, cloud firewall policy, egress control, private service connectivity or network segmentation

- Working knowledge of Kubernetes security and networking, including network policy, service identity and container hardening

- Experience with threat modeling and risk assessment for networked and multi cloud systems

- Track record of driving engineering excellence through high standards, constructive code reviews and mentorship

- Clear communicator who can translate technical concepts across organizational levels and bring clarity and ownership to ambiguous technical problems

- Low ego, high empathy engineer who attracts talent and supports diverse, inclusive teams

- Experience supporting fast-paced startup engineering teams

Strong candidates may also have experience with:

- Secured Kubernetes networking at scale (CNI, network policy, service mesh or mTLS rollouts) or worked in high-assurance environments where controls had to be evidenced, not just deployed

- Worked on interconnects and private connectivity between cloud providers and physical data centers, including management-plane and out-of-band network security

- Built network traffic visibility or exfiltration detection systems

- Exposure to large-scale distributed training and what it demands of a network

- Led cross-functional security initiatives and navigated complex organizational dynamics

- Managing infrastructure through automated configuration and policy enforcement

- Hardening containerized applications and enforcing security policies

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. 

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:

£255,000 — £325,000 GBP 

Logistics 

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you ----- addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different 

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us! 

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

title: Software Engineer, Lab Automation
description:
Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments. 

We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world.

We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today.

Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development.

We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.

About the Role

You'll build work-cell orchestration, instrument drivers, protocol scheduling, error-recovery logic, and monitoring. Physical systems fail in ways pure software doesn't — a plate gets stuck, a liquid handler skips a well, a temperature controller drifts. Your job is to make the system handle all of it gracefully. This is a broad, hands-on role for a strong engineer who wants their code to drive real machines and see it run the same day.

What You'll Do

- Build orchestration software that coordinates liquid handlers, plate readers, incubators, and robot arms — handling timing dependencies, state, and error recovery.

- Reverse-engineer and develop instrument drivers and APIs. Each instrument speaks a different protocol (serial, USB, TCP/IP); you work out how it talks and build a clean abstraction over it.

- Model and execute complex multi-step protocols reliably — a single run can span dozens of steps across multiple instruments.

- Build error-recovery logic so that when something fails mid-run, the system retries, skips, alerts, or pauses depending on the failure mode.

- Create monitoring and observability for work-cell health: instrument status, run progress, error rates.

- Debug across the software–hardware boundary — figuring out whether bad data is a comms, firmware, calibration, or code problem.

- Work closely with lab automation engineers, the rest of the software team, and the scientists running production.

Stack

TypeScript and Python, Postgres (Supabase), Modal for compute. We control instruments with open-source Python tooling like PyLabRobot and PyHamilton wherever we can, rather than proprietary vendor GUIs.

What We're Looking For

- Strong software engineering skills. You write production code in Python and/or TypeScript — well-structured and maintainable, not just prototypes.

- Comfortable at the hardware-software boundary. You've built software that drives physical devices, or you're excited to. You can read a protocol spec, debug a flaky connection, and reason about timing.

- Lab automation experience is a strong plus. Familiarity with PyHamilton, PyLabRobot, Opentrons, or similar tooling helps — as does a background in robotics, industrial automation, IoT, or embedded systems.

- Maker and hacker attitude. You like figuring out how closed systems work and building the thing that makes them work better. Bonus if you're comfortable with electronics, microcontrollers, or a 3D printer when an integration needs a physical fix.

- AI-native builder. It's 2026 — you build with coding agents like Claude Code as a default, and you have sharp judgment about what they produce.

- Self-starter and independent. You define what needs building from how the lab actually works, not just what's in the ticket.

- Reliability-minded. The lab runs 24/7; you design systems where one instrument failing doesn't cascade through the whole work cell.

Biology background not required — but you should be excited that the code runs real experiments.

Details

- Location: Lausanne, Switzerland (on-site — you need hands-on access to physical instruments).

- Type: Full time

- Start date: ASAP

Application deadline 

We are reviewing applicants on a rolling basis.

Bewerbung 

Schick uns deinen Lebenslauf und ein paar Zeilen zu einer Kampagne oder einem Launch, den du verantwortet hast. Was war das Ziel, was hast du getan, was kam dabei heraus? Ein Anschreiben brauchen wir nicht.

Wir bauen Roboter für alle, deshalb wollen wir ein Team, das das abbildet. Wir stellen nach Fähigkeiten ein und freuen uns ausdrücklich über Bewerbungen von Menschen, die in Marketing und Tech unterrepräsentiert sind. Wenn du nicht jeden Punkt erfüllst, aber denkst, das ist dein Job: bewirb dich.
