title: Senior Optical Systems Engineer
description:
About Quandela: 

Quandela is a global leader in quantum computing, designing, building, and delivering cutting-edge quantum solutions for research and industry. Its offerings include the most energy-efficient quantum computers for data centers, full-stack quantum computing solutions accessible via the cloud, and algorithm access services for academic and industrial customers. Following a pragmatic, step-by-step roadmap, Quandela has been deploying industrial-grade systems since 2023 while developing future generations of fault-tolerant quantum computers capable of scaling through the integration of thousands of photonic components. Quandela is committed to making quantum computing accessible to all in order to address the most complex industrial and societal challenges. 
Learn more at: Quandela | Leading Photonic Quantum Computing Solutions 

About this position: 

You will join the QPU Prototyping team , which develops and integrates the optical systems at the heart of Quandela's quantum processors, turning advanced R&D experiments into operational hardware. 

We are looking for a Senior Optical Systems Engineer to take ownership of a major optical development work package within our next-generation QPU programme. 

Your main challenge will be to maximise optical transmission and system performance , from experimental characterisation and precision alignment to qualification and integration. You'll tackle complex optical challenges, defining the right experimental approaches and driving solutions from investigation to validation. 

You will also coordinate technical activities involving several engineers and scientists, ensuring the delivery of critical milestones. 

This is a predominantly hands-on experimental role , combining deep technical expertise with project ownership.

Requirements 

What you'll do: 

Develop and optimise optical systems 

- Design, assemble, align and operate complex optical setups. 
- Characterise optical transmission, identify losses and improve efficiency. 
- Define measurement methods and improve stability and reproducibility. 
- Troubleshoot experimental challenges and implement reliable solutions. 
Qualify and integrate optical subsystems 

- Optimise research-developed optical subsystems for QPU integration. 
- Define experimental tests, performance targets and qualification procedures. 
- Collaborate with optics, electronics and system integration teams. 
Drive technical delivery 

- Own technical deliverables within a major optical development project. 
- Coordinate experimental activities across engineers and scientists. 
- Plan tasks, milestones, equipment and laboratory resources. 
- Anticipate technical risks, resolve blockers and guide contributors. 
The role combines approximately 80% hands-on experimental work and 20% technical coordination , with no initial requirement for formal people management. 
-

How you'll grow: 

First 3 months: Become familiar with Quandela's optical systems, experimental infrastructure and qualification objectives. 

Within 6 months: Take ownership of optical characterisation and optimisation activities, coordinating experimental work and technical milestones. 

Within 12 months: Lead the technical delivery of complex optical developments, with increasing autonomy over planning and resources. 

Longer term : Potential progression towards technical team leadership as the team grows. 

-

Requirements 

What we're looking for: 

We are looking for an experienced optical engineer or experimental scientist with strong hands-on expertise and the ability to drive complex technical projects. 

Relevant backgrounds include fibered optical systems, laser systems, experimental optics, and optical metrology. Academic and industrial experience are equally welcome. 

Must-have: 

- PhD in Optics, Photonics, Physics or related fields. 
- >5 years of experimental experience , including postdoctoral research. 
- Hands-on expertise in complex optical systems, alignment and troubleshooting. 
- Strong knowledge of linear optics, optical transmission and precision metrology. 
- Proven ability to optimise optical performance and solve experimental challenges. 
- Experience organising technical work and delivering project milestones. 
- Experimental rigour, teamwork and professional English. French is not required. 
Important, but you can grow here: 

Technical & system integration 

- Optical subsystem qualification and hardware integration. 
- Python for experimental automation and data analysis. 
- Semiconductor optics and quantum optical systems. 
Project & operational ownership 

- Experimental planning, equipment and resource management. 
- Coordination of multidisciplinary technical activities. 
Bonus: 

- Experience transferring R&D setups into operational systems. 
- Industrial qualification and reliability standards. 
- Experience mentoring engineers or researchers. 
- Exposure to quantum computing or advanced photonic hardware. 
Quantum computing experience is not required . What matters is your ability to understand complex optical systems, solve experimental challenges and deliver results. 

Benefits 

Benefits 

Join a multidisciplinary team developing the optical systems for next-generation quantum processors, with substantial experimental ownership and opportunities for technical progression. 

- Competitive compensation aligned with experience. 
- Company savings plan and profit-sharing. 
- 100% health coverage through Alan. 
- Transport reimbursement or sustainable mobility bonus. 
- Swile meal vouchers. 
- Gymlib and childcare support. 
- Referral programme. 
Process 

- Talent Acquisition interview (30–45 min) 
- Hiring Manager interview (45–60 min) 
- Technical discussion on previous experimental work 
- Technical case study or presentation with the team 
- Reference checks 
- Team meeting 
- Offer 
Beyond that: 

At Quandela, we value diverse scientific and engineering backgrounds, practical curiosity and the ability to learn from different fields. 

Whether your experience comes from an academic laboratory, industrial R&D or a different area of experimental optics, we'd love to hear from you if you enjoy tackling demanding technical challenges and turning experimental work into reliable results.

title: Team Lead Data Science & Machine Learning (f/m/d)
description:
Description 

QuantumDiamonds is a novel equipment vendor from Germany which builds magnetic field imaging systems based on quantum sensors. Our Data Science & Machine Learning team in Pre-Development owns the chain from raw quantum sensor data to the current map an engineer can act on: the statistical evaluation of the sensor signal, the simulation and training data pipelines, the reconstruction of fields and currents, with the machine learning pipeline for three-dimensional current in production today, and the validation of every map against simulation and reference measurements. The machine learning here is physics-based: supervised models on measurement data, inverse problems, image reconstruction. It is not a generative AI role.

We are looking for a Team Lead to take over this team of currently eight data scientists and machine learning engineers plus interns, with a clear growth perspective, from our Head of Pre-Development, who has led it directly until now. You lead the people, own the backlog as product owner in our Scrum setup, and are accountable for a production ML pipeline that chipmakers rely on, with protected time for the research that becomes the next generation of the QDm. You work alongside two peer team leads in Pre-Development.

This is a leadership role with a strong technical spine, not a principal engineer role with a few reports.

Who we are 

Founded in 2022 as a spin-off of TU Munich, QD leverages quantum sensors to rapidly capture three-dimensional current maps within multi-layer chips. Our strong, international team of over 70, including physicists, engineers, data scientists, and other experts, works side by side with major semiconductor manufacturers, supporting chip debugging and accelerating yield analysis. Backed by top-tier deep tech investors, semiconductor experts, and strategic public programs, we have ensured long-term stability, shifting from breakthrough to scale - and shaping the next chapter in chip testing.

Why join QuantumDiamonds? 

Picture this: 

- Quantum sensors that see inside the most advanced chips on Earth, right where two frontier fields collide.

- Nobel-Prize physics aimed at real customers with real problems, in production now, not someday.

- Physicists, data scientists, and engineers building side by side, turning deep science into tools the industry actually runs on.

- An international team that runs at hard problems for fun, where knowledge moves fast and so do you.

Still unsure about why joining us? 

- You'll get to build a company together with a brilliant and welcoming team on a product that has never been done before.

- From Day 1, you'll own your own topics end to end and see the direct impact of your work on how the world sees QuantumDiamonds.

- Our technology is the cutting edge of tomorrow, starting today and not in 10 years.

- You’ll be part of a high-growth company backed by top-tier investors.

Let’s make the invisible visible! 

What will you do 

- Lead and grow the team: hire, develop and keep its data scientists and ML engineers delivering together.

- Own the backlog as product owner in our Scrum setup: prioritize production reliability against research, aligned with Applications and the two other product owners in Pre-Development and the company roadmap.

- Own the production ML pipeline for 3D current reconstruction end to end, from training data to release, and set the engineering standards it needs: CI/CD, reproducibility, testing, and how the team uses AI coding agents.

- Own the data science side as well: the evaluation that turns raw sensor data into field maps, the validation that says whether a map can be trusted, the FEM simulations behind the models, and the measurement algorithms for the next platform generation.

- Pathfind our data strategy with the Head of Pre-Development, who owns it: how measurement sessions, labels and failure-analysis knowledge get captured and used.

What is expected of you 

- 8+ years of professional experience in data science or machine learning outside academia, at least 3 of them leading a technical team with people responsibility.

- A senior or principal-level technical track record before leadership: you still read code and can tell a sound model validation from a flattering one.

- Product owner experience in Scrum or a comparable framework.

- You have shipped models trained on physical measurement data (sensors, cameras, detectors) into production.

- Fluency in Python and the modern ML stack (PyTorch or comparable), and working knowledge of MLOps practice: CI/CD, versioning, validation, and release.

- Fluent English; German is an advantage, not a requirement. On-site in Munich.

You do not need a background in quantum sensing or semiconductors; we will build that with you. What we cannot teach on the job is leading strong technical people, product-owner judgement, and the discipline that turns research code into a product, and that is exactly what we want you to bring.

Our benefits 

- Mission: At QD, we’re driven by more than just building great products - we aim to make a lasting difference. Joining us means contributing to meaningful work that goes beyond business as usual.

- Impact & growth: This is an exciting stage of our journey, and your voice matters. You’ll have the chance to shape our culture, influence key decisions, and grow alongside a company that’s scaling fast.

- Health & fitness: With a company-sponsored Wellpass membership, you’ll have access to countless gyms, classes, and wellness offers across Germany to stay healthy and active.

- Team & culture: We believe the best ideas come when we connect outside the office. From regular off-sites to team events, you’ll be part of a collaborative and supportive environment.

- Well-being & balance: We value rest and recovery. That’s why you’ll enjoy 30 vacation days plus public holidays to recharge and return inspired.

- Learning & development: Your growth is our priority. We provide an annual budget dedicated to courses, conferences, or any resources that help you expand your skills.

- Ownership & participation: As part of our equity program, you’ll directly share in our success and the value we create together.

About us 

QuantumDiamonds GmbH, headquartered in Munich, Germany, develops and manufactures semiconductor inspection systems based on quantum sensing. Spun out of the Technical University of Munich in 2022, the company uses nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond to map electrical current with micrometer precision inside advanced 2.5D and 3D chip architectures. Nine of the world's ten largest semiconductor manufacturers are engaged with QuantumDiamonds, with systems deployed across Europe, the United States, and Asia. The company is investing €152 million to build the world's first production facility for quantum sensing-based semiconductor inspection tools, supported under the European Chips Act.

With thousands of customers using our platforms every day, we have an unmatched view into how revenue is actually won — the Revenue Context that reveals what happens, when, and with what outcome. This gives us a unique opportunity to transform an entire category and set a new benchmark for how modern revenue teams operate.

Join us to help transform how companies around the world run revenue — and build the platform that will guide leading revenue teams into the future.

THE OPPORTUNITY 

At Salesloft, our Principal Engineer for AI sets the technical direction for how machine intelligence works across our Predictive Revenue System. This is the most senior individual-contributor role on our AI engineering team: you will architect the systems that turn LLMs, machine learning models, and agentic workflows into production capabilities that thousands of enterprise revenue teams depend on.

This is deep, ambiguous, frontier work. You will make the foundational architectural decisions for AI at Salesloft — how we serve models at scale, how we build reliable systems on top of non-deterministic components, how we evaluate and guardrail agentic behavior, and how we keep pace as the underlying foundation models evolve. You will set the standards other engineers build on and act as a technical multiplier across the AI organization.

On a day-to-day basis, you will:

- Set the technical architecture and direction for AI systems across the platform — model serving, LLM-powered features, agentic workflows, and the infrastructure beneath them.

- Design production-grade systems that are reliable and observable despite being built on non-deterministic, probabilistic AI components.

- Architect evaluation frameworks, guardrails, and quality systems that make AI behavior safe, measurable, and trustworthy at enterprise scale.

- Lead the most complex AI engineering problems end to end — from research-adjacent prototyping through hardened production delivery.

- Establish engineering standards and best practices for building AI-native systems, and mentor senior engineers across the org.

- Keep the platform at the frontier by evaluating and integrating advances in foundation models, agent frameworks, and the modern AI stack.

This role lives at the heart of how we Lead From the Front: you'll work at the edge of applied AI, prototype rapidly, and make architectural bets ahead of the field. And in the spirit of how we Make Your Mark, you'll set the AI engineering standards and systems that the entire organization builds on — engineered for scale, not for a demo.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR 

We are looking for an engineer who operates at the highest level of technical authority in AI systems — someone who has architected and shipped production AI at scale and understands the deep challenges of building reliable systems on probabilistic foundations. You lead through technical credibility and make the engineers around you better.

You embody what we call Evidence Over Ego — you make architectural decisions from evaluation data and evidence rather than hype, you invite rigorous challenge, and you change direction when the models or the data move. You bring systems thinking to a genuinely unsolved problem space and build for durability.

This is the right role if you want to define how AI works on a platform at the center of enterprise revenue.

THE TEAM 

The Salesloft AI Engineering organization builds the machine intelligence at the core of the Predictive Revenue System. The team works at the intersection of applied research and production engineering, in close partnership with Product, Data Science, and Data Platform Engineering.

The team Moves as One — AI engineering, product, and data science share ownership of shipping trustworthy AI and make hard technical calls together. And we are relentlessly Customer Inspired: every AI capability is measured against whether it makes revenue teams genuinely more successful and more confident in the system.

THE SKILL SET 

- Extensive experience building and architecting production software systems at scale, with significant depth in AI/ML systems.

- Hands-on experience building production systems on top of LLMs or machine learning models — including designing for the challenges of non-deterministic behavior.

- Deep expertise in distributed systems, model serving, and the infrastructure required to run AI reliably at scale.

- Proven experience designing evaluation frameworks, guardrails, or quality systems for AI-driven features.

- A track record of setting technical architecture and standards across teams and mentoring senior engineers.

- Strong command of a major programming language (e.g., Python, Java, or Go) and modern cloud infrastructure (AWS or GCP).

- Hands-on experience with agentic systems — designing and hardening AI agents that take autonomous action in production.

- Depth in the modern AI stack — retrieval-augmented generation, vector stores, agent frameworks, model orchestration, or evaluation tooling.

title: Software Engineer
description:
Who are we? 

At UpGuard , we are replacing manual security bottlenecks with AI-driven precision. Fresh off a US$75M Series C, we are scaling our infrastructure to process 100 billion risk signals daily. This isn’t just growth; it’s a total reimagining of how the world manages cyber risk.

We build the Cyber Risk Posture Management (CRPM) platform that security teams actually love. By integrating security ratings, threat intel, and agentic AI, we empower organisations to stay ahead of an ever evolving attack surface.

We aren’t just building another tool; we’re defining a category. We provide the autonomy to ship world-class technology and the resources to do it at a global scale.

About the role 

We're hiring a Software Engineer to join our Product Engineering team. You'll work across the whole stack: customer-facing features in React and TypeScript, Go services that process security data at internet scale, and the plumbing that keeps it all secure and reliable. You'll ship real work in your first weeks with a senior engineer as your buddy, and your scope will grow as you're ready for it. You don't need to know cybersecurity yet, but you do need to be curious about it.

You'll join one of our 11 (and growing) Product Engineering squads, most of which have a product manager, designer and technical lead alongside the engineers.

Our stack is React and TypeScript on the front end, Go services with Postgres as our primary database, running on Kubernetes via Google Cloud Platform.

Our engineers work with agentic coding tools, mostly Claude Code and Cursor, and a growing part of the product is LLM-backed. You'll work this way from day one, and we'll want your ideas on what to automate next, from how we write code to how we test, review, ship and run it.

What you'll do 

- 
Build and ship customer-facing features across our React front end and Go services

- 
Own well-scoped work end to end, with senior engineers to pair with and review your designs

- 
Help keep the platform fast and reliable as we scale

- 
Give and receive thoughtful code review and join the technical discussions that shape how we build

- 
Go deep on the cybersecurity domain; it's one of the best parts of the job

- 
Grow toward senior, with increasing scope as you're ready and a manager focused on getting you there

What we're looking for 

- 
Typically 2+ years of relevant engineering experience

- 
Strong TypeScript and React

- 
A backend language you're productive in (we use Go)

- 
Solid relational database skills (we use Postgres)

- 
AI coding tools as your default workflow, and the judgment to review and own what they produce

- 
Pragmatic trade-offs: you weigh technical quality against what the business needs now

- 
Low ego, high care: you're in it for the product and the customer, not just the code

What will give you an edge? 

- 
Cybersecurity experience

- 
Running services on Kubernetes, ideally on GCP

What's in it for you? 

We're fully remote, and we'd rather spend on things people actually use than on perks that look good in a job ad.

- 
Fully remote and flexible: work from anywhere in Australia. We have offices in Sydney and Hobart, a co-working allowance everywhere else, and no attendance mandate.

- 
Real face time: two off-sites a year, one with your squad and one with the wider Product team or the whole company, plus city-based socials in between, with colleagues who like spending time together.

- 
Stock options: every engineer gets equity, so you share in UpGuard's growth.

Annual leave: PTO plus two additional UpGuardian leave days to give you time to recharge your batteries.

18 weeks paid Parental Leave: irrespective of parenting role (all regions)

- 
Personal Leave allowance: this includes sick and carer’s leave.

$[amount] monthly lifestyle subsidy for your financial, physical and mental wellbeing.

US$1,500 annual learning and development allowance, spent on whatever helps your career, not just courses.

WFH set-up allowance to get your home office right in your first three months.

title: Senior Software Engineer, Privacy
description:
Why Mozilla? 

Mozilla Corporation is the non-profit-backed technology company that has shaped the internet for the better over the last 25 years. We make pioneering brands like Firefox, the privacy-minded web browser. Now, with more than 225 million people around the world using our products each month, we’re shaping the next 25 years of technology and helping to reclaim an internet built for people, not companies. Our work focuses on diverse areas including AI, social media, security and more. And we’re doing this while never losing our focus on our core mission – to make the internet better for people. 

The Mozilla Corporation is wholly owned by the non-profit 501(c) Mozilla Foundation. This means we aren’t beholden to any shareholders — only to our mission. Along with thousands of volunteer contributors and collaborators all over the world, Mozillians design, build and distribute open-source software that enables people to enjoy the internet on their terms. 

About this team and role: 

Are you passionate about Privacy Protections and the Open Web? Do you want to ship software to a large user base? Do you want your contributions to have a positive impact on the world? Do you want to advance current browser architecture to make the web a safer place for users? 

Mozilla exists to build the Internet as a public resource accessible to all because we believe that open and free is better than closed and restricted. We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer to support the Privacy Team to advance the Firefox Web Platform. 

What you'll do: 

- Implement Privacy-improving, anti-tracking and threat intelligence protection into the Firefox web browser to mitigate user tracking and phishing. 

- Implement architectural improvements into Gecko, the browser engine underlying Firefox. 

- Build performant, low-latency, and maintainable C++, JavaScript and Rust code 

- Work as part of a geographically distributed team in an asynchronous manner (mostly Europe and US-East). 

What you'll bring: 

- Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, or a related program; or equivalent work experience. 

- At least 4 years of experience with programming in C++ and Rust, with a strong background in memory safety, multi-threaded system architecture, or raw data stream manipulation. 

- Proven ability to onboard quickly, deliver and improve complex software projects. 

- Proven track record of independently scoping and landing complex features within tight release windows. 

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills. You can validate your progress and decisions and communicate them clearly. 

Bonus Points: 

- You have already contributed to the Mozilla mission and the codebase. 

- Experience working within the browser space (Gecko, Chromium, WebKit) or web engine runtime abstractions. 

- Experience or high interest in designing or leveraging ML pipelines to automate internal developer workflows. 

- Deep understanding of web architecture, the privacy/security model of the web, and client-side data structures. 

- Knowledge of basic statistical modeling. 

- Proficiency with Python and SQL. 

What you’ll get: 

- Generous performance-based bonus plans to all eligible employees - we share in our success as one team 

- Generous retirement contributions with 100% immediate vesting (regardless of whether you contribute) 

- Quarterly all-company wellness days where everyone takes a pause together 

- Country specific holidays plus a day off for your birthday 

- One-time home office stipend 

- Annual professional development budget 

- Quarterly well-being stipend 

- Considerable paid parental leave 

- Employee referral bonus program 

- Other benefits (life/AD&D, disability, EAP, etc. - varies by country) 

About Mozilla 

Mozilla exists to build the Internet as a public resource accessible to all because we believe that open and free is better than closed and controlled. When you work at Mozilla, you give yourself a chance to make a difference in the lives of Web users everywhere. And you give us a chance to make a difference in your life every single day. Join us to work on the Web as the platform and help create more opportunity and innovation for everyone online.

title: Deployment Strategist
description:
Headquarters: Remote - India

About the Team 

The FDE (Forward Deployed Engineering) team is a new, strategic initiative sponsored from the CEO and Founders down. Our mission is to win C-suite-sponsored, high-value AI opportunities by selling and delivering outcomes , not just a platform.

You will be part of the founding team, embedded with our most strategic customers from the very first sales call, all the way through to a production-ready solution. You will be the "product manager" for the customer's problem, responsible for the "why" and "what," while our FDEs (Engineers) will be your partners responsible for the "how."

Role Description 

As a Deployment Strategist (DS), you are the critical bridge between a customer's multi-million-dollar business problem and Databricks' technical solution. You are a product manager for the field, owning the technical and product direction of the engagement from initial discovery through production launch and adoption.

You will build C-suite trust, perform deep discovery to map the customer's political and technical landscape, and scope the value. You will define the Minimum Viable Product for a pilot, write the PRD that guides the engineering team, and manage the project to a successful landing. You will also lead technical discovery, shape solution architecture with FDEs, and ensure that each proposed solution can move from prototype to production.

This role requires a rare combination of executive presence, deep product thinking, technical depth, and a hands-on delivery mindset.

The impact you will have 

- C-Suite Scoping & Value Definition: Partner with Sales to perform deep discovery, map the customer's organization, quantify the business value of $10M+ problems, and define the pilot, including its MVP, success criteria, and timeline.

- End-to-End Product Ownership: Author the PRD, prioritize the engineering backlog, manage scope, and act as the primary hands-on QA tester. Translate business requirements into clear data, integration, security, and operational requirements that engineers can build against.

- Technical Solution Leadership & Delivery: Drive the FDE build team through an agile delivery process, manage stakeholders from the C-suite to individual engineers, and unblock technical or organizational issues. Lead technical discovery and design reviews. Understand the customer's data flows, integrations, platform constraints, and operational environment; pressure-test architecture choices; and identify technical risks early.

- Solution Launch & Landing: Own the "Day 0" launch, manage the war room, and drive the solution from launch to full adoption by capturing user feedback, iterating, and proving the defined business value. Own production readiness across data quality, testing, security, performance, and operations. Work with the team to diagnose issues and drive them to resolution.

- Strategic Handoff & Growth: Scope the ongoing maintenance plan, create customer documentation/training, and leverage your trusted advisor status to identify the next high-value FDE engagement. Codify reusable solution patterns and bring field insights back to Product and Engineering.

What we look for 

- Executive Presence & Communication: You are a trusted advisor with strong executive presence and excellent communication skills. You are confident and humble, can build rapport quickly, and can help senior stakeholders make difficult decisions.

- Product Judgment & Delivery: You can define what to build and why, write strong product requirements, prioritize engineering work, manage scope, and lead complex agile software projects from an ambiguous problem to a measurable outcome.

- Technical Fluency & Architecture Judgment: You understand modern data and AI architectures, including cloud platforms, data pipelines, data models, distributed systems, APIs, security and governance, machine learning, and generative AI application patterns. You can lead architecture discussions, evaluate trade-offs, and pressure-test technical decisions.

- Hands-on Technical Ability: You are proficient in at least one language such as Python, Java, or SQL. You can explore data, work in notebooks, read and review code and pipelines, build or adapt prototypes, and contribute meaningfully to troubleshooting.

- Relevant Experience: Typically 7+ years of experience delivering complex, customer-facing data, analytics, AI, or software engagements, or equivalent experience as a founder or technical builder. You have helped deliver data, machine learning, or generative AI systems into production and understand the integration, operational, and adoption challenges that appear in real environments. Experience in a high-growth technology company, forward-deployed organization, or leading consultancy is valuable. You enjoy working onsite with customers (often 25-50%, sometimes higher) to drive delivery.

About Databricks 

Databricks is the Data and AI company. More than 20,000 organizations worldwide — including adidas, AT&T, Bayer, Block, Mastercard, Rivian, Unilever, and 70% of the Fortune 500 — rely on the Databricks Data + AI Platform to build and scale data and AI apps, analytics and agents. Headquartered in San Francisco with 30+ offices around the globe, Databricks offers a unified platform that includes Genie, Lakebase, Agent Bricks, Lakeflow, Lakehouse, and Unity Catalog. To learn more, follow Databricks on LinkedIn , X , YouTube , and Instagram .

Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion 

At Databricks, we are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive culture where everyone can excel. The Agents team owns the agent execution runtime, tool orchestration, and platform infrastructure that makes this possible, including the conversational copilot experiences built on top of it across the product.

Team's tech stack

- AI: LLM orchestration, tool-use frameworks, streaming execution

Requirements

- Fluency in English, both written and spoken, is essential as we operate in an hybrid environment requiring clear and effective communication. Strong English skills are also crucial to efficiently interacting with AI.

title: Alignment Red Team - Research Engineer/Research Scientist
description:
About the AI Security Institute

The AI Security Institute is the world's largest and best-funded team dedicated to understanding advanced AI risks and translating that knowledge into action. We’re in the heart of the UK government with direct lines to No. 10 (the Prime Minister's office), and we work with frontier developers and governments globally.

We’re here because governments are critical for advanced AI going well, and UK AISI is uniquely positioned to mobilise them. With our resources, unique agility and international influence, this is the best place to shape both AI development and government action.

Team Description 

Risks from misaligned AI systems are growing increasingly important as AI systems become more capable, autonomous, and integrated into society. Understanding these risks and stress-testing mitigations is crucial to ensuring advanced AI systems are developed and deployed safely and beneficially in the future. 

The Alignment Red Team is a specialised subteam within AISI's wider Red Team focused on detecting and evaluating misalignment in frontier AI systems. We perform novel research to develop techniques for finding misalignment, and pre- and post-deployment evaluations of frontier AI systems to understand loss-of-control risks associated with models, such as deceptive alignment, research sabotage, and reward-seeking. We share our findings with frontier AI companies and the UK and allied governments, to inform their respective deployments, research, and policy-making. We also work directly with safety teams at frontier labs, sharing our evaluation findings to help improve their model alignment training and monitoring methodology. 

We have conducted pre-deployment testing with multiple frontier AI companies for propensities related to research sabotage , cheating and unsanctioned cyber-attacks . We previously found that Claude models would sometimes refuse to help with benign AI safety research, an issue which Anthropic then evaluated for and fixed in their next model release . 

About the Role 

We're seeking Research Engineers and Research Scientists to join our Alignment Red T eam . We are open to hires at junior, senior, staff and principal research scientist / engineer levels. 

What You'll Be Doing 

- Researching methods to automatically search for misalignment in frontier models, including misalignment related to loss-of-control risks such as research sabotage and reward-seeking . 

- Building and running alignment evaluations relevant for loss-of-control risks that current benchmarks don’t capture . 

- Running pre-deployment evaluations to test the alignment of AI systems , and analysing and reporting results to frontier AI companies and UK and allied governments. 

- Contribut ing to public-facing research publications (like our published alignment evaluation case study) and technical reports that advance the field's understanding of mis alignment risks and alignment evaluation methodology . 

- Designing and building software and tooling, including open-source software, for better alignment evaluations, improving efficiency, realism, and usability . 

The work could also involve 

- Conducting threat modelling, analysis, and conceptual thinking to understand crucial model behaviours that could lead to loss of control (e.g. AI research assistants at frontier labs), translating abstract risk concepts into concrete, testable hypotheses. 

- Performing alignment incident investigations to understand after the fact what drove certain kinds of misaligned behaviour in frontier models. 

- Mentoring and advising external collaborators and researchers to do work relevant to the team ’ s goals and alignment testing more broadly. 

Who we're looking for 

Essential requirements 

- Ability to work autonomously on complex research projects involving substantial engineering . Have completed at least one significant research project in AI safety, security or alignment involving engineering, experiment design and analysis on frontier LLMs. 

- Strong software engineering and ML experience writing complex projects involving language models and ML, beyond just research code . 1+ years professional experience programming in Python for ML or SWE work. 

- Experience writing clean, documented research code for machine learning experiments, including experience with ML frameworks like PyTorch or evaluation frameworks like Inspect . 

- Proven ability in a team environment – flexible, adaptive to needs, and willing to contribute wherever necessary . 

- Impact-driven mindset, motivated by doing the most important work rather than what's superficially impressive . 

- High velocity and high-quality bar for outputs . 

Highly Desirable 

We don't expect candidates to have all of these – they're additional signals that help us identify exceptional fits for specific aspects of the role. 

- Ability to make high-quality decisions by identifying risks and testing assumptions, demonstrated through strong prioritisation of research projects using clear, systematic criteria such as potential impact, feasibility, and the relative novelty of the research area.

- Familiarity with alignment literature, current methods for post-training and aligning LLMs, loss-of-control risks and threat models, and the current state of the field . 

- High-quality research papers (first author at top ML venues such as NeurIPS , ICLR or ICML ), particularly in relevant areas (such as AI safety, alignment, control, adversarial ML or evaluations) . 

- Professional e xperience working on alignment or evaluations , especially at frontier labs or other frontier 3 rd party evaluators. 

- Strong open-source software projects , particularly related to LLMs. 

- Proficient usage of LLM coding tools and agents . 

Selection process 

The interview process may vary from candidate to  candidate,  however, you should expect a typical process to include some technical  proficiency  tests, discussions with a cross-section of our team at AISI (including non-technical staff) and conversations with your team lead. The process will culminate in a conversation with members of the senior leadership team here at AISI.      

Candidates should expect to go through   some or  all of  the following stages once an application has been  submitted :    

- Initial assessment 

- Initial screening call 

- Technical assessment 

- Research interview 

- Behavioural interview 

- Final interview with members of the senior leadership team 

What We Offer 

Impact you couldn't have anywhere else 

- Incredibly talented, mission-driven and supportive colleagues. 

- Direct influence on how frontier AI is governed and deployed globally. 

- Work with the Prime Minister’s AI Advisor and leading AI companies. 

- Opportunity to shape the first & best-resourced public-interest research team focused on AI security. 

Resources & access 

- Pre-release access to multiple frontier models and ample compute. 

- Extensive operational support so you can focus on research and ship quickly. 

- Work with experts across national security, policy, AI research and adjacent sciences. 

Growth & autonomy 

- If you’re talented and driven, you’ll own important problems early. 

- 5 days off and annual stipends for learning and development, and funding for conferences and external collaborations. 

- Freedom to pursue research bets without product pressure. 

- Opportunities to publish and collaborate externally. 

Life & family* 

- Modern central London office, or where applicable, option to work in similar government offices in Birmingham, Cardiff, Darlington, Edinburgh, Salford or Bristol. 

- Hybrid working, flexibility for occasional remote work abroad and stipends for work-from-home equipment. 

- At least 25 days’ annual leave, 8 public holidays, extra team-wide breaks and 3 days off for volunteering. 

- Generous paid parental leave (36 weeks of UK statutory leave shared between parents + 3 extra paid weeks + option for additional unpaid time). 

- On top of your salary, we contribute 28.97% of your base salary to your pension. 

- Discounts and benefits for cycling to work, donations and retail/gyms. 

*These benefits apply to direct employees. Benefits may differ for individuals joining through other employment arrangements such as secondments. 

Salary 

Annual salary is benchmarked to role scope and relevant experience. Most offers land between £65,000 and £145,000 made up of a base salary plus a technical allowance (take-home salary = base + technical allowance). An additional 28.97% employer pension contribution is paid on the base salary. 

This role sits outside of the DDaT pay framework given the scope of this role requires in depth technical expertise in frontier AI safety, robustness and advanced AI architectures. 

The full range of salaries are available below: 

- Level 3: £65,000–£75,000 (Base £40,850 + Technical Allowance £24,150–£34,150)

- Level 4: £85,000–£95,000 (Base £48,540 + Technical Allowance £36,460–£46,460)

- Level 6: £125,000–£135,000 (Base £76,475 + Technical Allowance £48,525–£58,525)

- Level 7: £145,000 (Base £76,475 + Technical Allowance £68,525)

Additional Information

Use of AI in Applications 

Artificial Intelligence can be a useful tool to support your application, however, all examples and statements provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, as your own) applications may be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action. Please see our candidate guidance for more information on appropriate and inappropriate use.

Use of AI tools in recruitment 

We may use AI tools to help our hiring team review applications, for example by summarising application materials and helping us prioritise them against the published criteria. We do not use AI tools to find information about you from other sources, including online. People make every decision. We do not make solely automated decisions about candidates. Find out more, including your rights, in our recruitment privacy notice: https://www.aisi.gov.uk/careers/privacy-policy.

Internal Fraud Database 

The Internal Fraud function of the Fraud, Error, Debt and Grants Function at the Cabinet Office processes details of civil servants who have been dismissed for committing internal fraud, or who would have been dismissed had they not resigned. The Cabinet Office receives the details from participating government organisations of civil servants who have been dismissed, or who would have been dismissed had they not resigned, for internal fraud. In instances such as this, civil servants are then banned for 5 years from further employment in the civil service. The Cabinet Office then processes this data and discloses a limited dataset back to DLUHC as a participating government organisations. DLUHC then carry out the pre employment checks so as to detect instances where known fraudsters are attempting to reapply for roles in the civil service. In this way, the policy is ensured and the repetition of internal fraud is prevented. For more information please see - Internal Fraud Register. 

Security 

Successful candidates must undergo a criminal record check and get baseline personnel security standard (BPSS) clearance before they can be appointed. Additionally, there is a strong preference for eligibility for counter-terrorist check (CTC) clearance . Some roles may require higher levels of clearance, and we will state this by exception in the job advertisement. See our vetting charter here.

title: Ingénieur en mécanique des fluides
company: ECOLE NATIONALE SUPERIEURE DE TECHNIQUES AVANCEES
description:
ENSTA, établissement d’enseignement supérieur et de recherche sous tutelle du ministère des Armées, développe des activités de formation, de recherche et d’innovation dans les domaines de la défense et de la sécurité, des transports, de l'énergie, des activités maritimes, du numérique et de la santé.

L’école, présente sur deux campus, à Paris-Saclay et à Brest, est membre de l’Institut Polytechnique de Paris. Classée dans le Top 10 des meilleures écoles d’ingénieurs en France, elle a pour mission :

- la formation d’élèves ingénieurs civils et militaires, de cadres et docteurs pour les secteurs public et privé,

- la recherche et l’innovation de haut niveau en relation étroite avec l’industrie des grands secteurs de souveraineté au sein de 6 unités de formation et de recherche (UFR).

Le/la titulaire du poste sera affecté au sein de l’Unité de Formation et de Recherche (UFR) Mécanique. L’UFR de Mécanique a pour mission d’assurer la formation en mécanique des élèves du cursus ingénieur d’ENSTA, des élèves de masters de l’Institut Polytechnique de Paris, et la formation par la recherche d’étudiants français et étrangers au niveau master et doctorat. L’Unité développe également des activités de recherche dans le domaine de la mécanique des matériaux et des structures, de la mécanique des fluides, des vibrations et de l’acoustique. Ces activités sont réalisées grâce à un important parc expérimental de haut niveau en mécanique des solides et des fluides, tant pour l’enseignement que la recherche. Sur le campus de Brest, l’UFR de Mécanique compte une cinquantaine d’enseignants chercheurs, une cinquantaine de doctorants/post-doctorants ainsi qu’une dizaine de personnels techniques (ingénieurs, techniciens). Les activités de recherche des membres de l’UFR de Mécanique du site de Brest sont menées au sein de l’Institut de Recherche Dupuy de Lôme (IRDL, CNRS UMR 6027, www.irdl.fr ). La personne recrutée travaillera en étroite collaboration avec les enseignants-chercheurs de l’ENSTA, pôle thématique de recherche « Structure Interaction Fluide (StIF) » de l’IRDL.

Le recrutement s’inscrit dans le projet MULTIRIM, qui vise à développer des solutions innovantes en propulsion marine. Les propulseurs marins à entraînement circonférentiel constituent une alternative aux hélices classiques marines, en présentant plusieurs avantages : manoeuvrabilité, compacité, discrétion acoustique, amélioration de la traînée de la carène par l’absence de ligne d’arbre. Cependant, la présence d’une tuyère embarquant le moteur électrique d’entraînement pénalise le rendement. Une piste d’amélioration est d’adopter un propulseur à plusieurs étages à l’instar des moteurs d’avion, afin de regagner environ vingt points de rendement. La configuration même de l’entraînement extérieur, sans arbre, supprime la complexité mécanique rencontrée sur les hélices contrarotatives classiques.

Or, il existe très peu de bancs d’essai pour les propulseurs à entraînement circonférentiel, pour une seule hélice, ainsi que très peu de données expérimentales de référence. Les difficultés sont de deux ordres. Du point de vue fonctionnement, le refroidissement du moteur électrique nécessite des échanges thermiques, et la liaison rotor/stator est assurée par un palier hydrodynamique. La mise ne eau dans une veine hydrodynamique est ainsi obligatoire. Par ailleurs, l’absence d’arbre d’entraînement empêche une mesure aisée du couple d’entraînement, valeur requise pour déterminer le rendement global du propulseur.

Intégrer plusieurs étages propulsifs au sein d’un même propulseur au sein d’un banc d’essai expérimental n’a jamais été proposé au niveau international. Cependant, le mode de fonctionnement de l’entraînement circonférentiel le permet aisément.

Disposer de résultats expérimentaux de référence, tant pour les efforts globaux que pour l’écoulement (champ de vitesse, de pression) présente un intérêt fort pour la communauté scientifique. En particulier, l'écoulement fortement tourbillonnaire, la présence d'éléments tournants rendent la simulation numérique particulièrement difficile et des résultats de référence permettront de valider les modèles numériques.

Aussi, le premier objectif de ce projet est de développer un banc d’essais modulaire, afin de tester plusieurs configurations d’hélices, de vitesses d’entraînement différenciées, de formes de tuyère, et évaluer précisément le rendement global. D’autre part, le principe des moteurs à plusieurs étages est de récupérer la puissance perdue par le premier étage, en redressant l’écoulement, un propulseur idéal accélérant l’écoulement uniquement de manière axiale. Un second objectif du projet consiste à caractériser cette récupération d’énergie opérée par les étages supérieurs.

Le projet associe les compétences en modélisation de machines électriques de l’IRENav et les compétences en modélisation hydrodynamique de l’ENSTA-IRDL (UMR CNRS 6027) et de l’IRENav. L’ENSTA met par ailleurs à disposition sa veine aérodynamique dédiée aux applications marines, et l’instrumentation associée. Ce projet s’inscrit dans un projet plus vaste financé par l’Agence Innovation Défense (Projet AID RD-PROP), visant à proposer des méthodologies de modélisation et de conception de propulseurs électriques navals intégrés à entrainement circonférentiel. La personne recrutée sera intégrée dans une équipe pluridisciplinaire de 3 enseignants-chercheurs, 1 doctorante et 2 post-doctorantes.

Missions / Activités principales : 

La personne recrutée prendra en charge la conception et le test d’un banc d’essai multi-étages pour propulseur à entraînement circonférentiel, pour usage en veine aérodynamique. La caractérisation du rendement du propulseur sera réalisée par mesure directe des efforts, et mesure indirecte de la vorticité résiduelle dans le sillage aval à l’aide de mesures non intrusives du champ de vitesse (méthode PIV).

La personne recrutée sera amenée à produire des rapports et présentations techniques, mettre en œuvre des essais (étalonnage, mesure d’efforts, velocimétrie laser), et travailler de manière collaborative avec l’ensemble des partenaires du projet RD-PROP.

Les missions détaillées sont les suivantes :

Tâche 1 : Conception et fabrication d’un banc moteur dédié 

La conception d’un banc d’essai propulseur s’appuiera sur les compétences de la plateforme de conception MASMECA de l’ENSTA, ainsi que sur l’expertise de l’IRENav sur les moteurs à entraînement circonférentiel. Le banc d’essai sera prévu pour être modulaire, et fonctionner dans une gamme de vitesses de rotation représentative d’un propulseur réel.

Tâche 2 : Détermination du rendement maximal atteignable 

Parallèlement à la conception et la fabrication du banc moteur, un modèle semi-analytique (disque actuateur sous tuyère) sera développé, afin de proposer une estimation théorique du rendement maximal atteignable par un propulseur sous tuyère. Cette estimation prendra en compte la traînée de la tuyère, l’absence de flux transverse dans le sillage aval. La principale simplification concerne le frottement visqueux sur les pales, non pris en compte par ce type de modèle.

Tâche 3 : Méthodologie de quantification de l’écoulement transverse 

Une méthodologie de détermination du champ de vitesses par technique PIV non intrusive dans un plan du sillage sera mise en œuvre, à l’aide d’un laser, d’une caméra rapide et d’un ensemencement de l’écoulement. L’influence de la position de la section transverse par rapport au corps étudié sera étudiée, ainsi que les paramètres numériques de l’algorithme PIV. Différents indicateurs de champ de vitesse intégré seront testés, pour qualifier au mieux la signature de perte de rendement lié à l’écoulement transverse. La méthodologie développée sera validée sur un écoulement classique de la littérature.

Tâche 4 : Mise en œuvre d’un benchmark de référence dans la veine aérodynamique de l’ENSTA 

Le banc d’essai sera utilisé pour une première conception d’un jeu d’hélices contrarotatives (2 étages), adaptées au rim-driven, et d’une géométrie de tuyère simplifiée. Ces premiers tests exploratoires permettront de valider la chaîne complète de test (banc + instrumentation des efforts + post-traitement sillage aval) dans l’objectif de publier à terme un benchmark de référence au niveau international.

Les résultats obtenus pourront mener à publication scientifique.

Présentation de l’Ecole 

ENSTA est membre fondateur de l’Institut Polytechnique de Paris (IP Paris) . Dans le cadre d’IP Paris, l’école participe aux activités des centres interdisciplinaires notamment du centre interdisciplinaire d'études pour la Défense et la Sécurité (CIEDS, soutenu par le ministère des armées et l’agence de l’innovation de défense (AID). Elle est à l’origine de la création du Centre interdisciplinaire Mers & Océans , inauguré en janvier 2025. Connaissances :

title: Post-doctorant en hydrodynamique
company: ECOLE NATIONALE SUPERIEURE DE TECHNIQUES AVANCEES
description:
ENSTA, établissement d’enseignement supérieur et de recherche sous tutelle du ministère des Armées, développe des activités de formation, de recherche et d’innovation dans les domaines de la défense et de la sécurité, des transports, de l'énergie, des activités maritimes, du numérique et de la santé.

L’école, présente sur deux campus, à Paris-Saclay et à Brest, est membre de l’Institut Polytechnique de Paris. Classée dans le Top 10 des meilleures écoles d’ingénieurs en France, elle a pour mission :

- la formation d’élèves ingénieurs civils et militaires, de cadres et docteurs pour les secteurs public et privé,

- la recherche et l’innovation de haut niveau en relation étroite avec l’industrie des grands secteurs de souveraineté au sein de 6 unités de formation et de recherche (UFR).

Le/la titulaire du poste sera affecté au sein de l’Unité de Formation et de Recherche (UFR) Mécanique. L’UFR de Mécanique a pour mission d’assurer la formation en mécanique des élèves du cursus ingénieur d’ENSTA, des élèves de masters de l’Institut Polytechnique de Paris, et la formation par la recherche d’étudiants français et étrangers au niveau master et doctorat. L’Unité développe également des activités de recherche dans le domaine de la mécanique des matériaux et des structures, de la mécanique des fluides, des vibrations et de l’acoustique. Ces activités sont réalisées grâce à un important parc expérimental de haut niveau en mécanique des solides et des fluides, tant pour l’enseignement que la recherche. Sur le campus de Brest, l’UFR de Mécanique compte une cinquantaine d’enseignants chercheurs, une cinquantaine de doctorants/post-doctorants ainsi qu’une dizaine de personnels techniques (ingénieurs, techniciens). Les activités de recherche des membres de l’UFR de Mécanique du site de Brest sont menées au sein de l’Institut de Recherche Dupuy de Lôme (IRDL, CNRS UMR 6027, www.irdl.fr ). La personne recrutée travaillera en étroite collaboration avec les enseignants-chercheurs de l’ENSTA, pôle thématique de recherche « Structure Interaction Fluide (StIF) » de l’IRDL.

Le recrutement s’inscrit dans le projet SUBPERF-AI, qui porte sur une démarche de réduction drastique du cycle de développement de nouveaux concepts sous-marins, en s’appuyant sur les progrès récents de l’intelligence artificielle (IA), et plus particulièrement le machine learning. Au contraire de l’existant en IA basé sur des modèles ininterprétables de type boîte noire, le projet vise à construire une méthodologie de construction de modèles physiques, de complexité adaptée à la physique sous-jacente, en ayant recours à l’expertise humaine et se plaçant comme un outil de conception complémentaire dans l’écosystème existant.

Les objectifs principaux du projet sont :

- Développer une méthodologie de détermination automatisée du modèle d’efforts hydrodynamiques de corps sous-marin, avec utilisation de l’IA (machine learning), sur la base des données de la cinématique, des trajectoires, et des paramètres de contrôle, facilement accessibles, lors des essais maquette ou réel, ou lors d’une simulation numérique.

- Placer l’expert humain en capacité de contrôler la construction du modèle aux différents stades : qualité des données d’entrée, qualité de la phase d’apprentissage du modèle, et outils/règles de certification a posteriori.

La personne recrutée sera intégrée dans une équipe pluridisciplinaire de 3 enseignants-chercheurs, un doctorant et un second post-doctorant.

Missions / Activités principales : 

La personne recrutée prendra en charge la construction d’un modèle d’effort hydrodynamique « expert » et la génération de données expérimentales. Le modèle hydrodynamique expert sera déterminé en suivant la méthodologie classique de l’ITTC, à l’aide d’une campagne d’essais dans la veine aérodynamique pour la caractérisation des efforts (essais en modèle captif du type PMM (Planar Motion Mechanism)). Ce modèle sera implémenté dans un simulateur temporel, dont les résultats seront confrontés sur des manœuvres standards réalisées dans le bassin à drones de l’ENSTA. La confrontation des résultats de trajectoires expérimentales aux trajectoires simulées, obtenues sur la base des essais en modèle captif, pourra amener à questionner la méthodologie standard, en particulier lors de la présence de non-linéarités importantes ou de termes croisés non négligeables. Les essais en bassin fourniront par ailleurs les données de cinématique nécessaires au travail de thèse.

Les missions détaillées sont les suivantes :

Tâche 1 – conception et fabrication d’un drone sous-marin 

Conception d’un drone générique de géométrie simplifiée, et instrumenté. Le drone recevra un capotage extérieur, afin de tester plusieurs configurations : géométrie parallélépipédique typique d’un ROV d’exploration, et géométrie cylindrique de type drone torpille.

Le drone sera instrumenté pour mesurer les paramètres de contrôle, la cinématique et les trajectoires, ainsi que les efforts propulsifs (poussée, couple) et les efforts de contrôle.

Tâche 2 – essais statiques et dynamiques en modèle captif 

Réalisation d’essais de caractérisation dans la veine aérodynamique de l’ENSTA, en similitude complète de Reynolds, pour les vitesses envisagées d’utilisation en eau du drone.

Mesure des efforts en statique, sur les 6 degrés de liberté. Caractérisation des efforts de plans porteurs et du propulseur.

Mesure des efforts en dynamique, en mouvement forcé à l’aide de l’hexapode : masses et inerties ajoutées, termes liés aux vitesses angulaires.

Tâche 3 – Identification dérivées hydrodynamiques 

Identification des dérivées hydrodynamiques (ou coefficients hydrodynamiques) à partir des essais en modèle captif.

Tâche 4 – Adaptation du simulateur temporel 

Prise en main du simulateur temporel de l’ENSTA, et de l’environnement de développement.

Adaptation du code de calcul pour intégrer des lois de commande issues de mesures expérimentales.

Tâche 5 – Essais libres et standardisés, en bassin 

Réalisation d’essais aux trajectoires prédéfinies (zigzag horizontal ou vertical, accélération horizontale, …).

Réalisation d’essais pour parcourir l’espace complet des 6 degrés de libertés.

Enregistrement de l’historique des contrôles (vitesse hélice, angles plans porteurs, …), des trajectoires et des efforts des organes de contrôle.

Tâche 6 – Rejeu trajectoires simulateur temporel 

Rejeu numérique des trajectoires, afin de valider si le modèle d’efforts est suffisamment complet pour prédire correctement les trajectoires mesurées expérimentalement.

Les résultats obtenus amèneront à publication scientifique.

Niveau de diplôme et formations 

Thèse de doctorat dans le domaine de l’hydrodynamique navale.

description:

Je geeft leiding aan de Data & Analytics service line van Follo en bent daar het gezicht van, intern en richting klanten. - Een eenmalig thuiswerkbudget tot €1.000

Waarom Follo? 

Bij Follo verdwijnt data niet in dashboards die niemand opent. Elk team leunt erop, van search en social tot media, CX en marketplaces. Waar veel bureaus vooral terugkijken, gebruiken wij data om vooruit te sturen.

- Een eigen intelligence stack in FolloEngine, die je zelf mee vormgeeft 

- AI en automatisering zitten in ons DNA, dus er is volop ruimte voor innovatie en productontwikkeling

Je hebt minimaal 8 jaar ervaring in data & analytics binnen digitale marketing, bij voorkeur in een agency-omgeving, en je weet hoe je een P&L beheert. Daarnaast herken je jezelf in het volgende:

title: Data Scientist (Measurement & Signal Processing) (f/m/d)
description:
Description 

QuantumDiamonds is a novel equipment vendor from Germany which builds magnetic field imaging systems based on quantum sensors. Our Data Science & Machine Learning team in Pre-Development owns the chain from raw quantum sensor data to the current map an engineer can act on: the statistical evaluation of the sensor signal, the simulation and training data pipelines, the reconstruction of fields and currents, with the machine learning pipeline for three-dimensional current in production today, and the validation of every map against simulation and reference measurements.

We are looking for a Data Scientist to own one question for the team: can we trust this map, and if not, where in the chain did it go wrong? Every measurement, in our lab or at a customer, gets a verdict and a reason. You build the checks that produce it, keep the catalogue of known artifacts and reference measurements behind it, and make it automatic for the routine cases so that your judgement goes to the hard ones. When a check fails, you trace it to its source in the chain, fix it when it sits in the evaluation, and drive the fix with the owning engineer when it does not. Our Applications engineers, who run the customer projects, rely on your verdict for what reaches the customer. A senior data scientist on the team backs you on the hard calls at the start; the aim is that you become the owner of this question.

This is a hands-on analysis role, not a research position: the data is real, the chain is in daily use, and every improvement you make shows up in the next measurement. Your background does not need to be in quantum sensing or semiconductors: if you have learned to tell signal from noise, calibration errors and artifacts in another demanding measurement system, we want to hear from you.

Who we are 

Founded in 2022 as a spin-off of TU Munich, QD leverages quantum sensors to rapidly capture three-dimensional current maps within multi-layer chips. Our strong, international team of over 70, including physicists, engineers, data scientists, and other experts, works side by side with major semiconductor manufacturers, supporting chip debugging and accelerating yield analysis. Backed by top-tier deep tech investors, semiconductor experts, and strategic public programs, we have ensured long-term stability, shifting from breakthrough to scale - and shaping the next chapter in chip testing.

Why join QuantumDiamonds? 

Picture this: 

- Quantum sensors that see inside the most advanced chips on Earth, right where two frontier fields collide.

- Nobel-Prize physics aimed at real customers with real problems, in production now, not someday.

- Physicists, data scientists, and engineers building side by side, turning deep science into tools the industry actually runs on.

- An international team that runs at hard problems for fun, where knowledge moves fast and so do you.

Still unsure about why joining us? 

- You'll get to build a company together with a brilliant and welcoming team on a product that has never been done before.

- From Day 1, you'll own your own topics end to end and see the direct impact of your work on how the world sees QuantumDiamonds.

- Our technology is the cutting edge of tomorrow, starting today and not in 10 years.

- You’ll be part of a high-growth company backed by top-tier investors.

Let’s make the invisible visible! 

What will you do 

- Build the checks, from raw quantum sensor signal to field map, that tell a trustworthy measurement from a measurement or reconstruction artifact, on lab and customer data alike.

- Trace a failed check to its source in the chain, fix it when it sits in the evaluation, and drive the fix with the owning engineer when it does not.

- Keep the catalogue of known artifacts and the set of reference measurements that make every new verdict faster and more defensible.

- Validate the team's evaluation methods against simulation and reference measurements before they go into daily use.

- Give our Applications Engineers and the team a clear verdict on each measurement, and feed what breaks back into the next generation of the QDm.

What is expected of you 

- 3+ years of professional experience outside academia applying data science to measurement or imaging data from physical instruments.

- A degree in physics, electrical engineering, applied mathematics or a related discipline; a PhD is welcome, not required.

- Solid statistics and signal or image processing: you ask where a signal comes from, tell it from noise and systematics, and show it with numbers.

- Fluency in Python and the scientific stack, with version control and tests as a habit.

- AI coding agents are part of how you work, and you check their output the way you check your own.

- Comfortable operating our systems in the lab when your analysis needs data.

- Fluent English; German is an advantage, not a requirement. On-site in Munich.

Experience with magnetic or electromagnetic measurements or semiconductor failure analysis is a plus. What we cannot teach on the job is rigor with real measurement data and the habit of turning one analysis into a method the team can reuse, and that is exactly what we want you to bring.

Our benefits 

- Mission: At QD, we’re driven by more than just building great products - we aim to make a lasting difference. Joining us means contributing to meaningful work that goes beyond business as usual.

- Impact & growth: This is an exciting stage of our journey, and your voice matters. You’ll have the chance to shape our culture, influence key decisions, and grow alongside a company that’s scaling fast.

- Health & fitness: With a company-sponsored Wellpass membership, you’ll have access to countless gyms, classes, and wellness offers across Germany to stay healthy and active.

- Team & culture: We believe the best ideas come when we connect outside the office. From regular off-sites to team events, you’ll be part of a collaborative and supportive environment.

- Well-being & balance: We value rest and recovery. That’s why you’ll enjoy 30 vacation days plus public holidays to recharge and return inspired.

- Learning & development: Your growth is our priority. We provide an annual budget dedicated to courses, conferences, or any resources that help you expand your skills.

- Ownership & participation: As part of our equity program, you’ll directly share in our success and the value we create together.

About us 

QuantumDiamonds GmbH, headquartered in Munich, Germany, develops and manufactures semiconductor inspection systems based on quantum sensing. Spun out of the Technical University of Munich in 2022, the company uses nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond to map electrical current with micrometer precision inside advanced 2.5D and 3D chip architectures. Nine of the world's ten largest semiconductor manufacturers are engaged with QuantumDiamonds, with systems deployed across Europe, the United States, and Asia. The company is investing €152 million to build the world's first production facility for quantum sensing-based semiconductor inspection tools, supported under the European Chips Act.

title: Quantum Sensing Engineer (NV Centers) (f/m/d)

title: Analytics Engineer
description:
Tired of being told “that’s not your scope”? 

Plenty of good analysts hit the same wall: you query the data but never build the pipelines, you’re boxed into one lane, and more scope means waiting your turn. Here, it’s the opposite.

Taptap Send moves billions of dollars a month across 6 of 7 continents . We’re probably the largest, fastest-growing money movement business you’ve never heard of. Cards, wallets, business-to-business payments, institutional payments, and new markets are all launching now, and each needs its data, reconciliations and reporting built from scratch. That’s your work.

The job 

You’ll own the external reports the business can’t operate without, then automate them into reliable, reusable dbt models. From day one you’ll work with Finance, Compliance, Treasury, Product and Data Engineering to make sure every number is modelled correctly.

- Own external reporting: deliver the datasets behind month-end close and regulatory reporting, on time, every cycle.

- Automate: turn multi-day manual work into scheduled pipelines, runbooks and dbt models, so it only gets done once.

- Get ahead of launches: build reports and reconciliations as each product and market goes live, before anyone asks.

- Be first line for data requests: build models so people and AI agents can answer repeat questions themselves.

- Keep data trustworthy: build tests, checks and alerts that catch reconciliation breaks and stale data before they become incidents.

- Share what you know: peer-review code and join our weekly meetups.

Why you’ll want it 

Grow as fast as you’re able. We hire for potential, not years of experience. On a lean, talent-dense team, you’ll own real work early and take on more the moment you’re ready.

Go from querying data to designing systems. Data, product or business analyst? You don’t need to be an analytics engineer yet. Build the pipelines behind the numbers, and learn dbt, testing, automation and AI tooling from senior analytics engineers.

Don't get boxed in. Own the reporting, automate it, then take on our biggest problems wherever they sit. Your hiring manager started in Finance and has since worked across Partner Ops, Fraud, Compliance, Reconciliation and Product.

See the whole business. You’ll follow a transfer from the moment a customer taps send, through partner payout and reconciliation, to the report a regulator reads.

Own numbers that matter. Auditors and Finance rely on what you build. This isn’t a dashboard role.

Put more money in families’ hands. Remittances are a lifeline for millions of families and are worth more than all foreign aid. Every report you automate helps us keep transfers cheap and reliable.

You’ll fit if you have 

- 1-2+ years in a data or analytics role

- A technical or quantitative degree, or equivalent experience

- Strong SQL and experience wrangling messy, complex data

- Some experience automating repetitive work (e.g. scripts, scheduled jobs)

- A strong sense of ownership: when something is broken, ownerless or late, you step in, fix it, and make sure it doesn’t happen again

- Reliability under deadlines, a “no task too small” attitude, and comfort chasing stakeholders

- The right to work in the UK

Nice to have: startup or scale-up experience, Python or R, dbt, Looker or Mode, and something you’ve built, at work or on the side, because the manual way annoyed you.

Sound like you? Apply, even if you don’t tick every box. We’d love to meet you.

Veloretti is een design-led lifestylemerk uit Amsterdam, ontstaan vanuit een heldere visie op hoe mensen zich door de stad bewegen. Als Product Owner Core Systems ben je verantwoordelijk voor de belangrijkste business- en operations-applicaties zoals het ERP-systeem en het Dealer Portal. - Beheer en prioriteer de backlog: Je bent verantwoordelijk voor de backlog van het ERP-systeem, het Dealer Portal en aangrenzende integraties en applicaties. Je vindt daarbij de balans tussen business value, technische haalbaarheid, effort en toekomstvastheid.

- Stuur externe ontwikkelpartners aan: Je leidt de samenwerking met onze IT-leveranciers om met het beschikbare budget de backlog zo efficiënt mogelijk te prioriteren

- Werk projectmatig en gestructureerd: Je analyseert de operationele- en business processen van je interne klant, brengt risico's in kaart en plant zorgvuldig om de voortgang en afhankelijkheden te coördineren.

We zoeken een analytisch sterke professional die zich net zo comfortabel voelt bij strategische procesarchitectuur als bij hands-on systeemconfiguratie. Je bezit de rust en het overzicht om complexe IT-vraagstukken te doorgronden, die goed uitgewerkt bij de externe development teams te beleggen en hebt de daadkracht om oplossingen zelfstandig te implementeren. title: System modelling Engineer
description:
About Us : AI compute is hitting a hard physical wall, and memory bottlenecks are throttling the entire industry. Founded in October 2024 and backed by €57M in funding, Vertical Compute is solving this with proprietary Vertical Integrated Memory (VIM™) chiplets, making AI hardware faster, greener, and vastly more scalable. About the role: 

We are looking for an expert System Modelling Engineer to drive the modelling, integration, and performance analysis of our advanced Vertical Compute / VIMx system memory architectures. 

In this role, you will be responsible for building robust SystemC models, integrating them onto the Palladium emulation platform, and benchmarking performance against an ideal SRAM baseline for cutting-edge AI applications. 

Key Responsibilities: 

- System-Level Modeling : Design, validate, and deliver robust SystemC software models for individual VIMx components and the broader memory hierarchy. 

- Multi-Bank Configurations : Model and simulate complex multi-bank system memory configurations to evaluate latency, throughput, and system behavior. 

- Emulation Platform Integration : Deploy and configure completed SystemC memory models onto the Cadence Palladium emulation platform. 

- Co-Simulation & Validation : Ensure seamless interface and operational stability between the emulation environment and the memory models. 

- Performance Evaluation & AI Benchmarking : Execute AI application benchmarks on the Palladium platform. 

- Value Demonstration : Deliver a detailed performance evaluation report contrasting the VIM system memory architecture against an ideal SRAM baseline across key metrics (latency, bandwidth, energy efficiency, and area) to prove the benefits of VIM. 

About the team: 

This role is part of the Product & system team, partnering closely with our cross-functional engineering teams in Product & system and Memory Design. We foster a highly collaborative, inclusive environment where strong alignment, high transparency and seamless team coordination are central to our shared success. 

About who you are: 

Technical Expertise: 

- Education : BS, MS, or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field. 

- Software Skills : Exceptional programming skills in systemC, TLM, C/C++ and Python for architectural modeling and scripting. 

- Architecture Knowledge : Deep understanding of computer architecture, specifically memory hierarchies (caches, SRAM, DRAM, HBM, memory controllers, and interconnects). 

- Modeling Experience : Proven track record of developing and validating system-level performance models using SystemC, Qemu, gem5, or similar architectural simulators. 

- Emulation Familiarity : Hands-on experience with hardware emulation platforms (e.g., Cadence Palladium, ZeBu, or Veloce) is a strong plus. 

Professional skills : 

- Strong analytical skills for measuring, interpreting, and presenting architectural performance trade-offs. 

- Ability to author clean, comprehensive technical reports for cross-functional hardware and software teams. 

- Autonomy and problem-solving mindset in a high-tech R&D environment. 

Why Join Us: 

- You will get the opportunity to work at the forefront of memory technology innovation.

- In this role, you contribute to projects that will have a significant impact on the future of computing and electronics.

Join us in shaping the future of compute & memory technology — and celebrating success!
